content.text:
The two routes, briefly:

Quick / live (do it all on the phone). Convert your model to USDZ, AirDrop it to the iPhone, and open it in Reality Composer (free from Apple). You anchor the character to a real surface, walk around it for parallax, and hit record — done. If you have a Pro / LiDAR iPhone it adds contact shadows and occlusion, which is what sells the "it's really sitting there" look for a 2 cm figure.

Pro / post (better realism, more control). Film with CamTrackAR — it records your video plus a matched 3D camera track. You then import the original GLB into Blender or After Effects, line it up to that track, and render the character composited in. More steps, but you get full control over lighting and shadows so all five SuperClaws match the scene.

Either way the conversion to USDZ is the gate, and that's the part I can just do for you. Reality Converter (free Mac app) does it one-off, but I also have Blender connected here — so if you drop one of your FBX or GLB files in, I can convert it to a correctly-scaled 2 cm USDZ you can AirDrop straight to your phone.

Want me to set that up? Two quick things would help:

options.label: Live on phone (Recommended)
options.description: Simplest. Convert to USDZ, place in Reality Composer, record on the iPhone. Best for fast SuperClaws shots.

options.label: Pro / post compositing

content.text:
Perfect setup — Pro phone + live route is the sweet spot. With LiDAR you get real shadows and occlusion, so a 2 cm figure will actually look like it's standing on the table.

Here's your repeatable workflow once a model is in USDZ:

Get the USDZ onto the phone (AirDrop, or drop it in iCloud Drive / Files). Open Reality Composer → new project → Horizontal anchor → the "+" → import your USDZ. Because it's scaled to 2 cm it'll drop in at real size — a believable little figurine, not a giant prop. Point the phone at your surface so the dots lock onto it, tap to place the character, then use the AR record button (top right) and move slowly around it. Slow moves + good light = the LiDAR shadow grounds it.

A few things that make the 2 cm scale read as real: shoot from low and close (figure height, not standing-over-it), keep the phone moving for parallax, and avoid pure overhead — side angles show the shadow best.

To batch all five SuperClaws, make one Reality Composer scene per character (or place several in one scene and toggle visibility) so you can re-shoot any of them without rebuilding.

The only blocker is the conversion, and that's mine to handle. Drop one of your FBX or GLB files into the chat and I'll convert it to a correctly-scaled 2 cm USDZ and hand it back ready to AirDrop. Want to start with one character as a test, or send all five?

I searched across all your Little SuperClaws channels (there's no "Superdubs" — closest are #little-superclaws-series-, #little-super-claws-demo, #master-little-super-claws-project, etc.). Here's the honest result:

No actual 3D file of the blue character is up there. What's in Slack is:

A lot of blue character renders, but they're all flat PNG images — e.g. "001_A_blue_round-headed_claymation_character…", "009_In_a_claymation_style_a_small_round_blue…", "005_A_blue_claymation_character_with_a_red_suit…". Those are 2D pictures, not something AR can place.

3D-adjacent material, but it's R&D docs, not models: napkin-splat-pipeline.pdf and Meshy_to_Gaussian_Splat_RnD_Report.pdf. No FBX, GLB, USDZ, OBJ or .blend file anywhere in the workspace.

So for the AR workflow we're missing the one input that matters. Two ways forward:

If the FBX/GLB exists somewhere else (your Mac, Meshy account, Google Drive), drop it in here and I'll convert it to a 2 cm USDZ. Those R&D PDFs suggest you've been running a Meshy → 3D pipeline, so the file may live in Meshy rather than Slack.

Or, if no 3D file exists yet, we can make one: pick the best blue PNG and run it through image-to-3D (Meshy, which your own pipeline already uses) to generate a GLB, then I convert that to USDZ for the phone.

Want me to pull up the best blue character image so you can pick one to turn into 3D, or will you grab the FBX/GLB from Meshy?

Sources:
- [#little-superclaws-series- and related channels](https://napkin-world.slack.com/archives/C0B8VL34X7A)
- [napkin-splat-pipeline.pdf](https://napkin-world.slack.com/files/U04MZH76K5E/F0B3WECJ7JT/napkin-splat-pipeline.pdf)

"created using meshy api and presented using blender" — showcase_carousel.mp4 and showcase_lineup.mp4

{"files":[{"canAddChildren":false,"contentSnippet":"# index.html

Little Super Claws - Pitch Deck

LITTLE SUPER CLAWS

Five heroes. Ten claws. Zero impulse control.

Created by Laurence O'Byrne

1

THE HOOK

What if superheroes were made of clay,

had crab claws instead of hands,

and were fully aware they were AI-generated?

That's Little Super Claws.

2

LOGLINE & FORMAT

LOGLINE

Five claymation misfits with crab claws protect Claw City from villains who are somehow even more dysfunctional than they are.

FORMAT

Episode Length: 7 minutes

Style: Claymation (AI-generated)

Format: Adult Comedy

Platform: Streaming/VOD

3

THE META ANGLE

Made by AI. Starring AI. For humans... for now.

AI-generated characters with self-aware humor. The show IS the proof of concept for AI entertainment. Audiences don't just watch the show—they experience the future of animation.

4

THE HEROES

G

The anxious leader

Wait... did we plan this?

The Spire

Cool strategist

I have a plan. Maybe.

Hops-Gear

Tech gadget nerd

I'll science the heck out of this.

Captain Quiff

Overconfident showboat

I've got this. Spoiler: I don't.

Red-Snapper

Hot-headed muscle

SMASH FIRST, QUESTIONS LATER\!

5

CHARACTER DEEP DIVE: THE TEAM

G - THE ANXIOUS LEADER

Personality: Wants to save the day but second-guesses everything

Role: Reluctant leader of the squad

Why he's funny: His anxiety is relatable; his crab claws make it absurd

Confidence: 3/10

THE SPIRE - STRATEGIST

Personality: Cool, collected... but his plans always backfire

Role: Tactician who overthinks simple problems

Why he's funny: His serious tone while wearing a domino mask is hilarious

Confidence: 9/10 (unwarranted)

6

CHARACTER DEEP DIVE: THE REST

HOPS-GEAR - TECH NERD

Personality: Optimistic, builds unnecessarily complex gadgets

Role: Q-like inventor with crab claws

Why he's funny: His contraptions are more trouble than they solve

Confidence: 8/10

CAPTAIN QUIFF - SHOWBOAT

Personality: Vain, overconfident, terrible in actual combat

Role: Comic relief who causes 50% of the problems

Why he's funny: His failures are immediate and catastrophic

Confidence: 11/10

7

CLAW CITY

Hero Lair

A converted claw machine in the warehouse district

Pincer Plaza

Downtown shopping district. Where villains shop, apparently.

The Shell

The city's most exclusive nightclub. Very hard to get in.

Snappertons

Rival hero team's base. There's an ongoing turf war.

Dr. Squid's Lab

Where the weird stuff happens. Always underground.

Tidepooled Tavern

Where heroes go to brood and drink terrible decisions

8

SEASON 1: 8 EPISODES

Ep 1

Ep 1: Origin Story (or lack thereof)

How did we get our claws? Nobody knows.

Ep 2

Ep 2: The Snappertons Strike

Meet our rivals. They're somehow worse.

Ep 3

Ep 3: Hops' "Perfect" Invention

Everything goes wrong, immediately.

Ep 4

Ep 4: Captain Quiff Goes Viral

TikTok fame corrupts absolutely.

Ep 5

Ep 5: Invasion of the Soft Crabs

AI-generated villains worse than heroes.

Ep 6

Ep 6: The Spire's Master Plan

It's convoluted. It fails spectacularly.

Ep 7

Ep 7: G's Crisis of Confidence

Can he save the city if he doesn't trust himself?

Ep 8

Ep 8: Team Up (Or Break Up?)

Season finale. Cliffhanger ending (literally).

9

TONE & MARKET POSITION

Bluey's Heart

Emotional storytelling. Character development. Genuine moments.

Robot Chicken's Chaos

Absurdist humor. Pop culture jokes. Rapid-fire gags.

Shaun the Sheep's Craft

Physical comedy. Detailed claymation. Slapstick brilliance.

10

INTERACTIVE AI: RUNWAY INTEGRATION

THE GAME CHANGER

Real-time avatar API lets audiences TALK to the characters. Not just watching—participating. Interactive AI entertainment.

WHY IT MATTERS

✓ Unique engagement

✓ Social sharing

✓ Repeat viewership

✓ User-generated content

✓ Monetization via interactions

✓ Proof-of-concept for AI entertainment

11

MARKET OPPORTUNITY

$28B+

Kids/Family Animation Market

Booming

Adult Animation (Rick & Morty, Invincible)

Next Wave

AI-Generated Content

Little Super Claws sits at the intersection of all three markets.

12

REVENUE STREAMS

Episodes (Streaming/VOD)

Merchandise (Toys, Apparel, Collectibles)

cd /sessions/trusting-sweet-feynman/mnt/uploads && ls -la *.glb && echo "---" && pip install pygltflib --break-system-packages -q 2>/dev/null; python3 - <<'PY'
import struct, json, os
for f in ["clawd.glb","decklan.glb","deirdre.glb","gerald.glb","nessa.glb"]:
    p=f
    with open(p,'rb') as fh:
        magic=fh.read(4); ver,length=struct.unpack('<II',fh.read(8))
        # read first chunk (JSON)
        clen,ctype=struct.unpack('<II',fh.read(8))
        js=json.loads(fh.read(clen))
    meshes=js.get('meshes',[])
    prims=sum(len(m.get('primitives',[])) for m in meshes)
    acc=js.get('accessors',[])
    # vertex count from POSITION accessors
    vcount=0
    for m in meshes:
        for pr in m.get('primitives',[]):
            pi=pr.get('attributes',{}).get('POSITION')
            if pi is not None: vcount+=acc[pi]['count']

import struct, zlib, os, sys, io
import numpy as np
import trimesh, fast_simplification
from scipy.spatial import cKDTree

def write_usdz(out_path, usda_text, tex_name, tex_bytes):
    files=[('model.usda', usda_text.encode('utf-8')), (tex_name, tex_bytes)]
    buf=io.BytesIO(); central=[]
    for name,data in files:
        nb=name.encode(); crc=zlib.crc32(data)&0xffffffff
        header_end=buf.tell()+30+len(nb); pad=(-header_end)%64; extra=b'\x00'*pad
        local_off=buf.tell()
        buf.write(struct.pack('<IHHHHHIIIHH',0x04034b50,20,0,0,0,0,crc,len(data),len(data),len(nb),len(extra)))
        buf.write(nb); buf.write(extra); buf.write(data)
        central.append((nb,crc,len(data),local_off))
    cd_start=buf.tell()
    for nb,crc,sz,off in central:
        buf.write(struct.pack('<IHHHHHHIIIHHHHHII',0x02014b50,20,20,0,0,0,0,crc,sz,sz,len(nb),0,0,0,0,0,off)); buf.write(nb)
    cd_size=buf.tell()-cd_start
    buf.write(struct.pack('<IHHHHIIH',0x06054b50,0,0,len(central),len(central),cd_size,cd_start,0))
    open(out_path,'wb').write(buf.getvalue())

def build_usda(name, P, idx, N, UV, tex_name):
    emn=P.min(0); emx=P.max(0)
    pts=', '.join('(%g, %g, %g)'%(x,y,z) for x,y,z in P)
    nrm=', '.join('(%g, %g, %g)'%(x,y,z) for x,y,z in N)
    st=', '.join('(%g, %g)'%(u,v) for u,v in UV)
    fvc=', '.join(['3']*(len(idx)//3))
    fvi=', '.join(map(str, idx.tolist()))
    return f'''#usda 1.0
(
    defaultPrim = "{name}"
    metersPerUnit = 1
    upAxis = "Y"
)

def Xform "{name}" (kind = "component")
{{
    def Mesh "geom"
    {{
        float3[] extent = [({emn[0]:g}, {emn[1]:g}, {emn[2]:g}), ({emx[0]:g}, {emx[1]:g}, {emx[2]:g})]
        int[] faceVertexCounts = [{fvc}]
        int[] faceVertexIndices = [{fvi}]
        point3f[] points = [{pts}]
        normal3f[] primvars:normals = [{nrm}] (interpolation = "vertex")
        texCoord2f[] primvars:st = [{st}] (interpolation = "vertex")
        uniform token subdivisionScheme = "none"
        rel material:binding = </{name}/mat>
    }}
    def Material "mat"
    {{
        token outputs:surface.connect = </{name}/mat/pbr.outputs:surface>
        def Shader "pbr"
        {{
            uniform token info:id = "UsdPreviewSurface"
            color3f inputs:diffuseColor.connect = </{name}/mat/tex.outputs:rgb>
            float inputs:roughness = 0.5
            float inputs:metallic = 0
            float inputs:occlusion = 1
            int inputs:useSpecularWorkflow = 0
            token outputs:surface
        }}
        def Shader "stReader"
        {{
            uniform token info:id = "UsdPrimvarReader_float2"
            token inputs:varname = "st"
            float2 outputs:result
        }}
        def Shader "tex"
        {{
            uniform token info:id = "UsdUVTexture"
            asset inputs:file = @{tex_name}@
            float2 inputs:st.connect = </{name}/mat/stReader.outputs:result>
            float4 inputs:scale = (1,1,1,1)
            token inputs:sourceColorSpace = "sRGB"
            token inputs:wrapS = "repeat"
            token inputs:wrapT = "repeat"
            float3 outputs:rgb
        }}
    }}
}}
'''

def process(glb, out, name, target=40000, target_h=0.02):
    m=trimesh.load(glb, process=False)
    g=list(m.geometry.values())[0] if isinstance(m,trimesh.Scene) else m
    V=np.asarray(g.vertices,dtype=np.float64); F=np.asarray(g.faces,dtype=np.int64)
    UV=np.asarray(g.visual.uv,dtype=np.float64)
    img=g.visual.material.baseColorTexture
    bio=io.BytesIO(); img.save(bio,format='JPEG',quality=92); tex=bio.getvalue()
    ext='jpg'; tex_name=f'{name}_tex.{ext}'
    tri0=len(F)
    Vd,Fd=fast_simplification.simplify(V.astype(np.float32),F.astype(np.int32),target_count=target)
    Vd=Vd.astype(np.float64); Fd=Fd.astype(np.int64)
    # UV remap via nearest original vertex
    tree=cKDTree(V); _,nn=tree.query(Vd,k=1); UVd=UV[nn].copy()
    UVd[:,1]=1.0-UVd[:,1]
    # scale + center + feet to floor
    mn=Vd.min(0); mx=Vd.max(0); h=mx[1]-mn[1]; s=target_h/h
    cx=(mn[0]+mx[0])/2; cz=(mn[2]+mx[2])/2
    Vd[:,0]=(Vd[:,0]-cx)*s; Vd[:,2]=(Vd[:,2]-cz)*s; Vd[:,1]=(Vd[:,1]-mn[1])*s
    tm=trimesh.Trimesh(Vd,Fd,process=False); N=np.asarray(tm.vertex_normals,dtype=np.float64)
    usda=build_usda(name,Vd,Fd.reshape(-1),N,UVd,tex_name)
    write_usdz(out,usda,tex_name,tex)
    print(f'{name}: {tri0}->{len(Fd)} tris, {len(Vd)} verts, tex {len(tex)/1e6:.1f}MB -> {os.path.getsize(out)/1e6:.1f}MB')

if __name__=='__main__':
    process(sys.argv[1],sys.argv[2],sys.argv[3])
PY

## Key API Endpoints

The Auto-Rigging and Animation API provides endpoints for submitting and retrieving character rigging tasks.

### Rigging Endpoint

The rigging endpoint allows you to create a new rigging task for a given 3D model, and upon successful completion, it provides a rigged character in standard formats and optionally basic walking/running animations.

- A 3D model for Meshy to rig via a publicly accessible URL or Data URI
- The approximate height of the character model in meters, which aids in scaling and rigging accuracy

### Animation Endpoint

The animation endpoint allows you to create a new task to apply a specific animation action to a previously rigged character, including post-processing options.

**POST /openapi/v1/animations** - Key parameters include:
- The id of a successfully completed rigging task, from which the character will be animated
- The identifier of the animation action to apply, with a complete list available in the Animation Library Reference

## Important Limitations

Programmatic rigging and animation currently only works well with standard humanoid (bipedal) assets with clearly defined limbs and body structure. Models with more than 300,000 faces are not supported for rigging when using input_task_id.

## PBR Texture Maps Generated by Meshy AI

Meshy outputs complete texture sets — Albedo, Normal, Roughness, and Metallic maps — so your assets react to lighting correctly out of the box.

Meshy supports PBR textures—Diffuse, Roughness, Metallic, and Normal maps—export-ready for Unreal, Unity, Blender, Maya, and WebGL.

Additionally, PBR Maps (metallic, roughness, normal) are generated in addition to the base color, and an emission map is also included when ai_model is meshy-6 or latest.

For more comprehensive PBR generation, Meshy can produce studio-quality PBR textures—including diffuse, normal, metallic, roughness, and ambient occlusion maps—instantly from text or image inputs.

## GLB Export Format

Meshy offers export in FBX, GLB, OBJ, STL, 3MF, USDZ, BLEND formats for production use. For maintaining PBR data integrity, for PBR fidelity, stay in GLB format, as OBJ + MTL doesn't carry PBR, and textures will export, but the metalness/roughness won't survive.

## Resolution Details

The base color texture can be generated at 4K (4096×4096) resolution for higher detail (only supported when ai_model is meshy-6 or latest), while PBR maps are always generated at 2K.

# Auto-Rigging & Animation API

The Auto-Rigging & Animation API allows you to programmatically rig 3D models and apply animations to them using Meshy's backend capabilities. This section provides the necessary details to integrate these features into your application.

Please note that programmatic rigging and animation currently only works well with standard humanoid (bipedal) assets with clearly defined limbs and body structure at this time.

---

## [Auto-Rigging API](#auto-rigging-api)

Endpoints for submitting and retrieving character rigging tasks. Rigging involves creating an internal skeleton (armature) and binding the model's mesh (skin) to it, making it ready for animation.

---

POST/openapi/v1/rigging

## [Create a Rigging Task](#create-a-rigging-task)

This endpoint allows you to create a new rigging task for a given 3D model. Upon successful completion, it provides a rigged character in standard formats and optionally basic walking/running animations.

Currently, auto-rigging is not suitable for the following models:

* Untextured meshes
* Non-humanoid assets
* Humanoid assets with unclear limb and body structure

When using `input_task_id`, models with more than **300,000 faces** are not supported for rigging. Please use the [Remesh API](https://docs.meshy.ai/en/api/remesh) to reduce the face count before rigging.

### Parameters

#### Required attributes

* Name
  :   `input_task_id`

  Type
  :   string

  Description
  :   The input task that needs to be rigged. Required if `model_url` is not provided. We currently support textured humanoid models.

      Only one of `input_task_id` or `model_url` may be used as input for rigging.
* Name
  :   `model_url`

  Type
  :   string

  Description
  :   Please provide a 3D model for Meshy to rig via a publicly accessible URL or Data URI. We currently support textured humanoid GLB files (`.glb` format). Required if `input_task_id` is not provided.

      Only one of `input_task_id` or `model_url` may be used as input for rigging.
      If both are supplied, then the `input_task_id` will be used by default.

#### Optional attributes

* Name
  :   `height_meters`

  Type
  :   number

  Description
  :   The approximate height of the character model in meters. This aids in scaling and rigging accuracy. It must be a positive number. Default: `1.7`.
* Name
  :   `texture_image_url`

  Type
  :   string

  Description
  :   The model's UV-unwrapped base color texture image. Publicly accessible URL or Data URI. We currently support `.png` formats.

### Returns

The `result` property of the response contains the task `id` of the newly created rigging task.

### Failure Modes

* Name
  :   `400 - Bad Request`

  Description
  :   The request was unacceptable. Common causes:

      + **Missing parameter**: Either `model_url` or `input_task_id` must be provided.
      + **Invalid model format**: The `model_url` points to a file with an unsupported extension (only .glb supported).
      + **Unreachable URL**: The `model_url` could not be downloaded.
      + **Invalid input task**: The `input_task_id` does not refer to a valid API task.
      + **Face count exceeded**: The input model has more than 300,000 faces. Please use the [Remesh API](https://docs.meshy.ai/en/api/remesh) to reduce the face count before rigging.
* Name
  :   `401 - Unauthorized`

  Description
  :   Authentication failed. Please check your API key.
* Name
  :   `402 - Payment Required`

  Description
  :   Insufficient credits to perform this task.
* Name
  :   `422 - Unprocessable Entity`

  Description
  :   Pose estimation failed. The provided model may not be a valid humanoid character.
* Name
  :   `429 - Too Many Requests`

  Description
  :   You have exceeded your rate limit.

## [The Rigging Task Object](#the-rigging-task-object)

The Rigging Task object represents the work unit for rigging a character.

### Properties

* Name
  :   `id`

  Type
  :   string

  Description
  :   Unique identifier for the task.
* Name
  :   `type`

  Type
  :   string

  Description
  :   Type of the Rigging task. The value is `rig`.
* Name
  :   `status`

  Type
  :   string

  Description
  :   Status of the task. Possible values: `PENDING`, `IN_PROGRESS`, `SUCCEEDED`, `FAILED`, `CANCELED`.
* Name
  :   `progress`

  Type
  :   integer

  Description
  :   Progress of the task (0-100). `0` if not started, `100` if succeeded.
* Name
  :   `created_at`

  Type
  :   timestamp

  Description
  :   Timestamp (milliseconds since epoch) when the task was created.

      A timestamp represents the number of milliseconds elapsed since January 1, 1970 UTC, following
      the [RFC 3339](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc3339) standard.
      For example, Friday, September 1, 2023 12:00:00 PM GMT is represented as `1693569600000`. This applies
      to **all** timestamps in Meshy API.
* Name
  :   `started_at`

  Type
  :   timestamp

  Description
  :   Timestamp (milliseconds since epoch) when the task started processing. `0` if not started.
* Name
  :   `finished_at`

  Type
  :   timestamp

  Description
  :   Timestamp (milliseconds since epoch) when the task finished. `0` if not finished.
* Name
  :   `expires_at`

  Type
  :   timestamp

  Description
  :   Timestamp (milliseconds since epoch) when the task result assets expire and may be deleted.
* Name
  :   `task_error`

  Type
  :   object

  Description
  :   Error object if the task failed, otherwise an object with an empty message string.

      + Name
        :   `message`

        Type
        :   string

        Description
        :   Detailed error message. Empty if task succeeded.
* Name
  :   `result`

  Type
  :   object

  Description
  :   Contains the output asset URLs if the task `SUCCEEDED`, `null` otherwise.

      + Name
        :   `rigged_character_fbx_url`

        Type
        :   string

        Description
        :   Downloadable URL for the rigged character in FBX format.
      + Name
        :   `rigged_character_glb_url`

        Type
        :   string

        Description
        :   Downloadable URL for the rigged character in GLB format.
      + Name
        :   `basic_animations`

        Type
        :   object (optional)

        Description
        :   Contains URLs for default animations. (e.g. if `generate_basic_animations` was implicitly true or enabled by default).

            - Name
              :   `walking_glb_url`

              Type
              :   string

              Description
              :   Downloadable URL for walking animation in GLB format (with skin).
            - Name
              :   `walking_fbx_url`

              Type
              :   string

              Description
              :   Downloadable URL for walking animation in FBX format (with skin).
            - Name
              :   `walking_armature_glb_url`

              Type
              :   string

              Description
              :   Downloadable URL for walking animation armature in GLB format.
            - Name
              :   `running_glb_url`

              Type
              :   string

              Description
              :   Downloadable URL for running animation in GLB format (with skin).
            - Name
              :   `running_fbx_url`

              Type
              :   string

              Description
              :   Downloadable URL for running animation in FBX format (with skin).
            - Name
              :   `running_armature_glb_url`

              Type
              :   string

              Description
              :   Downloadable URL for running animation armature in GLB format.
* Name
  :   `preceding_tasks`

  Type
  :   integer

  Description
  :   The count of preceding tasks in the queue. Meaningful only if status is `PENDING`.

## [Create an Animation Task](#create-an-animation-task)

This endpoint allows you to create a new task to apply a specific animation action to a previously rigged character. Includes post-processing options.

### Parameters

#### Required attributes

* Name
  :   `rig_task_id`

  Type
  :   string

  Description
  :   The `id` of a successfully completed rigging task (from `POST /openapi/v1/rigging`). The character from this task will be animated.
* Name
  :   `action_id`

  Type
  :   integer

  Description
  :   The identifier of the animation action to apply. See the [Animation Library Reference](https://docs.meshy.ai/api/animation-library) for a complete list of available animations.

#### Optional attributes

* Name
  :   `post_process`

  Type
  :   object

  Description
  :   Parameters for post-processing animation files.

      + Name
        :   `operation_type`

        Type
        :   string (required)

        Description
        :   The type of operation to perform. Must be one of:

            - `change_fps` (adjusts frame rate)
            - `fbx2usdz` (converts FBX to USDZ)
            - `extract_armature` (extracts armature)
      + Name
        :   `fps`

        Type
        :   integer (optional)

        Description
        :   The target frame rate. Default: `30`. Applicable only when `operation_type` is `change_fps`. Allowed values: `24`, `25`, `30`, `60`.

### Returns

The `result` property of the response contains the task `id` of the newly created animation task.

### Failure Modes

* Name
  :   `400 - Bad Request`

  Description
  :   The request was unacceptable. Common causes:

      + **Missing parameter**: `rig_task_id` or `action_id` is missing.
      + **Invalid rig task**: The `rig_task_id` is invalid or refers to a failed/non-existent task.
      + **Invalid action ID**: The `action_id` does not correspond to a valid animation.
* Name
  :   `401 - Unauthorized`

  Description
  :   Authentication failed. Please check your API key.
* Name
  :   `402 - Payment Required`

  Description
  :   Insufficient credits to perform this task.
* Name
  :   `404 - Not Found`

  Description
  :   The rigging task specified by `rig_task_id` was not found.
* Name
  :   `429 - Too Many Requests`

  Description
  :   You have exceeded your rate limit.

### Request

cURLJavaScriptPython

POST

/openapi/v1/animations

```
curl https://api.meshy.ai/openapi/v1/animations \
  -X POST \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${YOUR_API_KEY}" \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d '{
    "rig_task_id": "018b314a-a1b5-716d-c222-2f1776f7f579",
    "action_id": 92,
    "post_process": {
      "operation_type": "change_fps",
      "fps": 60
    }
  }'
```

## [The Animation Task Object](#the-animation-task-object)

The Animation Task object represents the work unit for applying an animation to a rigged character.

### Properties

* Name
  :   `id`

  Type
  :   string

  Description
  :   Unique identifier for the task.
* Name
  :   `type`

  Type
  :   string

  Description
  :   Type of the Animation task. The value is `animate`.
* Name
  :   `status`

  Type
  :   string

  Description
  :   Status of the task. Possible values: `PENDING`, `IN_PROGRESS`, `SUCCEEDED`, `FAILED`, `CANCELED`.
* Name
  :   `progress`

  Type
  :   integer

  Description
  :   Progress of the task (0-100).
* Name
  :   `created_at`

  Type
  :   timestamp

  Description
  :   Timestamp (milliseconds since epoch) when the task was created.

      A timestamp represents the number of milliseconds elapsed since January 1, 1970 UTC, following
      the [RFC 3339](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc3339) standard.
      For example, Friday, September 1, 2023 12:00:00 PM GMT is represented as `1693569600000`. This applies
      to **all** timestamps in Meshy API.
* Name
  :   `started_at`

  Type
  :   timestamp

  Description
  :   Timestamp (milliseconds since epoch) when the task started processing. `0` if not started.
* Name
  :   `finished_at`

  Type
  :   timestamp

  Description
  :   Timestamp (milliseconds since epoch) when the task finished. `0` if not finished.
* Name
  :   `expires_at`

  Type
  :   timestamp

  Description
  :   Timestamp (milliseconds since epoch) when the task result assets expire.
* Name
  :   `task_error`

  Type
  :   object

  Description
  :   Error object if the task failed, otherwise an object with an empty message string.

      + Name
        :   `message`

        Type
        :   string

        Description
        :   Detailed error message. Empty if task succeeded.
* Name
  :   `result`

  Type
  :   object

  Description
  :   Contains the output animation URLs if the task `SUCCEEDED`.

      + Name
        :   `animation_glb_url`

        Type
        :   string

        Description
        :   Downloadable URL for the animation in GLB format.
      + Name
        :   `animation_fbx_url`

        Type
        :   string

        Description
        :   Downloadable URL for the animation in FBX format.
      + Name
        :   `processed_usdz_url`

        Type
        :   string

        Description
        :   Downloadable URL for the processed animation in USDZ format.
      + Name
        :   `processed_armature_fbx_url`

        Type
        :   string

        Description
        :   Downloadable URL for the processed armature in FBX format.
      + Name
        :   `processed_animation_fps_fbx_url`

        Type
        :   string

        Description
        :   Downloadable URL for the animation with changed FPS in FBX format (e.g., if `change_fps` operation was used).
* Name
  :   `preceding_tasks`

  Type
  :   integer

  Description
  :   The count of preceding tasks in the queue. Meaningful only if status is `PENDING`.

### Example Animation Task Object

# Rigging API

The Rigging API allows you to programmatically add a skeleton (armature) to 3D humanoid models, binding the mesh to it so they are ready for animation. For applying animations to a rigged character, see the [Animation API](https://docs.meshy.ai/en/api/animation).

Please note that programmatic rigging currently only works well with standard humanoid (bipedal) assets with clearly defined limbs and body structure at this time.

---


POST/openapi/v1/rigging

## [Create a Rigging Task](#create-a-rigging-task)

This endpoint allows you to create a new rigging task for a given 3D model. Upon successful completion, it provides a rigged character in standard formats and optionally basic walking/running animations.

Currently, auto-rigging is not suitable for the following models:

- Untextured meshes
- Non-humanoid assets
- Humanoid assets with unclear limb and body structure


When using `input_task_id`, models with more than **300,000 faces** are not supported for rigging. Please use the [Remesh API](https://docs.meshy.ai/en/api/remesh) to reduce the face count before rigging.

When using `model_url`, the character's face must point toward the +Z axis (the standard glTF forward direction). Models facing other axes will fail pose estimation.

### Parameters

Only one of `input_task_id` or `model_url` is **required**. If both are provided, `input_task_id` takes priority.

-

Name
input_task_id

Type
string

Required

Description
The input task that needs to be rigged. We currently support textured humanoid models.

-

Name
model_url

Type
string

Required

Description
Please provide a 3D model for Meshy to rig via a publicly accessible URL or Data URI. We currently support textured humanoid GLB files (`.glb` format).

-

Name
height_meters

Type
number

default 1.7

Description
The approximate height of the character model in meters. This aids in scaling and rigging accuracy. It must be a positive number.

-

Name
texture_image_url

Type
string

Description
The model's UV-unwrapped base color texture image. Publicly accessible URL or Data URI. We currently support `.png` formats.

### Returns

The `result` property of the response contains the task `id` of the newly created rigging task.

### Failure Modes

-

Name
`400 - Bad Request`

Description
The request was unacceptable. Common causes:

  * **Missing parameter**: Either `model_url` or `input_task_id` must be provided.
  * **Invalid model format**: The `model_url` points to a file with an unsupported extension (only .glb supported).
  * **Unreachable URL**: The `model_url` could not be downloaded.
  * **Invalid input task**: The `input_task_id` does not refer to a valid API task.
  * **Face count exceeded**: The input model has more than 300,000 faces. Please use the [Remesh API](https://docs.meshy.ai/en/api/remesh) to reduce the face count before rigging.

-

Name
`401 - Unauthorized`

Description
Authentication failed. Please check your API key.

-

Name
`402 - Payment Required`

Description
Insufficient credits to perform this task.

-

Name
`422 - Unprocessable Entity`

Description
Pose estimation failed. The provided model may not be a valid humanoid character.

-

Name
`429 - Too Many Requests`

Description
You have exceeded your rate limit.

### Request

Python

POST

    "model_url": "YOUR_MODEL_URL_OR_DATA_URI",

  }'

timestamp

Description
Timestamp (milliseconds since epoch) when the task was created.

  
      A timestamp represents the number of milliseconds elapsed since January 1, 1970 UTC, following
the [RFC 3339](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc3339) standard.
For example, Friday, September 1, 2023 12:00:00 PM GMT is represented as `1693569600000`. This applies

Step-by-step guide for using sound effects in ElevenLabs.

[DevelopersLearn how to integrate sound effects into your application.](https://elevenlabs.io/docs/eleven-api/guides/cookbooks/sound-effects)[API referenceFull API reference for the Sound Effects endpoint.](https://elevenlabs.io/docs/api-reference/text-to-sound-effects/convert)

### Prompting guide

#### Simple effects

For basic sound effects, use clear, concise descriptions:

- “Glass shattering on concrete”
- “Heavy wooden door creaking open”
- “Thunder rumbling in the distance”


#### Complex sequences

For multi-part sound effects, describe the sequence of events:

- “Footsteps on gravel, then a metallic door opens”
- “Wind whistling through trees, followed by leaves rustling”
- “Sword being drawn, then clashing with another blade”


#### Musical elements

The API also supports generation of musical components:

- ”90s hip-hop drum loop, 90 BPM”
- “Vintage brass stabs in F minor”
- “Atmospheric synth pad with subtle modulation”


#### Audio terminology

Common terms that can enhance your prompts:

- **Impact**: Collision or contact sounds between objects, from subtle taps to dramatic crashes
- **Whoosh**: Movement through air effects, ranging from fast and ghostly to slow-spinning or rhythmic
- **Ambience**: Background environmental sounds that establish atmosphere and space
- **One-shot**: Single, non-repeating sound
- **Loop**: Repeating audio segment
- **Stem**: Isolated audio component
- **Braam**: Big, brassy cinematic hit that signals epic or dramatic moments, common in trailers
- **Glitch**: Sounds of malfunction, jittering, or erratic movement, useful for transitions and sci-fi
- **Drone**: Continuous, textured sound that creates atmosphere and suspense


## Key facts

- **Maximum duration**: 30 seconds per generation
- **Output formats**: MP3 for all effects; WAV at 48 kHz for non-looping effects
- **Looping effects**: Designed for seamless repeat playback — no audible start or end point
- **Musical elements**: Drum loops, bass lines, and melodic samples can be generated; for full music production use the [Music](https://elevenlabs.io/docs/overview/capabilities/music) API

## Texture Resolution Support

Meshy can generate base color textures at 4K (4096×4096) resolution for higher detail, while PBR maps are always generated at 2K. 4K base color generation is only supported when the ai_model is meshy-6 or latest.

## Retexture Functionality

Meshy Retexture applies new PBR texture maps to existing 3D models based on text-guided instructions or style images, generating texture maps including base color, roughness, and metalness for an existing 3D mesh.

## PBR Maps Generated

Every generated texture includes PBR maps — albedo, normal, roughness, and metallic — so assets look stunning under any lighting condition. The output includes downloadable URLs for the base color map, metallic map, normal map, roughness map, and emission map images.

## Download Formats

When satisfied, textured models can be downloaded in 7 formats (FBX, OBJ, GLB, USDZ, STL, BLEND, 3MF) ready for engines, renderers, or slicers.

## Input Model Formats

Meshy accepts 3D models for texturing in supported formats: .glb, .gltf, .obj, .fbx, .stl.

Finetunes are currently only available for Music v1. Music v2 Finetunes are coming. Existing v1
Finetunes are not compatible with Music v2, so plan migrations accordingly.

Standard music generation can produce high-quality tracks, but outputs may vary significantly in instrumentation, texture, production style, and feel. Finetunes grounds generation in your specific audio identity. Once trained, every track generated with your Finetune reflects the tone, structure, and character of your dataset - while remaining a new, original composition.

Finetunes addresses three core challenges in AI music generation:

- Brands cannot build a proprietary sound with prompting alone
- Creators cannot reliably replicate their style across projects
- Musicians exploring new ideas want outputs that feel authentic to their body of work


By fine-tuning on your tracks, the custom Finetune you create captures stylistic patterns across instrumentation, tempo, production style, timbre, and vocal character.

### How it works

- Upload non-copyrighted tracks - we automatically screen them for copyright compliance
- The Finetune is ready for use in approximately 5-10 minutes
- You generate music using your custom Finetune inside ElevenCreative


Qualifying Enterprise customers may fine-tune on proprietary intellectual property that they fully
own and control, without third-party copyright screening. This is designed for organizations with
catalogs they exclusively own. Contact your account manager to enable this capability.

### Curated Finetunes

In addition to custom training, ElevenCreative includes curated Finetunes created by ElevenLabs across global genres and styles, including:

- Afro House Beats
- Reggaeton
- Arabic Groove
- 70s Cambodian Rock
- 80s Nu-Disco Revival
- Mozart-Style Symphony


These are available instantly to eligible subscribers. No uploads required.

## Usage

Eleven Music is available today on the ElevenLabs website. The Music API is available for paid subscribers, with integration into our Agents Platform coming soon.

Created in collaboration with labels, publishers, and artists, Eleven Music is cleared for nearly all commercial uses, from film and television to podcasts and social media videos, and from advertisements to gaming. For more information on supported usage across our different plans, [see our music terms](https://elevenlabs.io/music-terms).

## Key facts

**###### What is Music v2?**

Music v2 is the next generation of ElevenLabs’ AI music model, with improved prompt adherence,
composition, prompt understanding, and multilingual output over Music v1. New capabilities
include long-form section-by-section composition, mid-track genre transitions, fast rap and
complex vocal delivery, improved inpainting, and sound effects embedded inside tracks.

**###### Is Music v1 still available?**

Music v1 will remain available during a transition period. Music v2 is the new default model in
the UI. For API generations, Music v1 will remain the default model for transition period. After
this, Music v2 will be the default in both UI and API. When Music v1 is deprecated, this will be
with at least a few months’ notice.

**###### How does inpainting work?**

In the UI, select a specific section of a generated song and regenerate just that section
without affecting the rest of the track. Inpainting quality is improved in v2.

**###### What's the maximum duration for generated music?**

Generated music has a minimum duration of 3 seconds and a maximum duration of 5 minutes.

**###### Is there an API available?**

Yes, refer to the [developer quickstart](https://elevenlabs.io/docs/eleven-api/guides/cookbooks/music) for more
information.

**###### Can I use Eleven Music for my business?**

Yes, Eleven Music is cleared for nearly all commercial uses, from film and television to
podcasts and social media videos, and from advertisements to gaming. For more information on
supported usage across our different plans, [see our music terms](https://elevenlabs.io/music-terms).

**###### What audio formats are supported?**

Generated audio is available in MP3 (44.1kHz, 128-192kbps) and WAV formats.

# Retexture API

Retexture API is a feature that allows you to integrate Meshy's AI retexturing capabilities into your own application. In this section, you'll find all the information
you need to get started with this API.

---


POST/openapi/v1/retexture

## [Create a Retexture Task](#create-a-retexture-task)

This endpoint allows you to create a new Retexture task. Refer to [The Retexture Task Object](#the-retexture-task-object) to see which
properties are included with Retexture task object.

### Parameters

Only one of `input_task_id` or `model_url` is **required**. If both are provided, `input_task_id` takes priority.

-

Name
input_task_id

Type
string

Required

Description
The ID of the completed Image to 3D or Text to 3D task you wish to retexture.
This task must be one of the following tasks: Text to 3D Preview, Text to 3D Refine, Image to 3D or Remesh. In addition, it must have a status of `SUCCEEDED`.

-

Name
model_url

Type
string

Required

Description
Provide a 3D model for Meshy to texture. Supported formats: `.glb`, `.gltf`, `.obj`, `.fbx`, `.stl`.

    There are two ways to provide the model:

  * **Publicly accessible URL**: A URL that is accessible from the public internet.
  * **Data URI**: A base64-encoded data URI of the model. Use MIME type `application/octet-stream`. Example: `data:application/octet-stream;base64,<your base64-encoded model data>`.

Only one of `text_style_prompt` or `image_style_url` is **required**. If both are provided, `image_style_url` takes priority.

-

Name
text_style_prompt

Type
string

Required

Description
Describe your desired texture style of the object using text. Maximum 600 characters.

-

Name
image_style_url

Type
string

Required

Description
Provide a 2d image to guide the texturing process. We currently support `.jpg`, `.jpeg`, and `.png` formats.

    There are two ways to provide the image:

  * **Publicly accessible URL**: A URL that is accessible from the public internet
  * **Data URI**: A base64-encoded data URI of the image. Example of a data URI: `data:image/jpeg;base64,<your base64-encoded image data>`
  
      Image texturing may not work optimally if there are substantial geometry differences between the original asset and uploaded image.

-

Name
ai_model

Type
string

default latest

Description
ID of the AI model to use for retexturing. Available values: `meshy-5`, `meshy-6`, `latest` (Meshy 6).

-

Name
enable_original_uv

Type
boolean

default false

Description
Use the original UV of the model instead of generating new UVs. When
enabled, Meshy preserves existing textures from the uploaded model.
If the model has no original UV, the quality of the output might not be as good.

-

Name
enable_pbr

Type
boolean

default false

Description
Generate PBR Maps (metallic, roughness, normal) in addition to the base color. An emission map is also included when `ai_model` is `meshy-6` or `latest`.

-

Name
hd_texture

Type
boolean

default false

Description
Generate the base color texture at 4K (4096×4096) resolution for higher detail.

  
      Only supported when `ai_model` is `meshy-6` or `latest`. PBR maps are always generated at 2K.

-

Name
remove_lighting

Type
boolean

default true

Description
Removes highlights and shadows from the base color texture, producing a cleaner result that works better under custom lighting setups.

  
      Only supported when `ai_model` is `meshy-6` or `latest`.

-

Name
target_formats

Type
string[]

Description
Specifies which 3D file formats to include in the output. Only the requested formats will be generated and returned, which can reduce task completion time. When omitted, all supported formats are included.

    Available values: `glb`, `obj`, `fbx`, `stl`, `usdz`, `3mf`

  
      When omitted, all formats except `3mf` are generated. `3mf` is only included when explicitly specified.

-

Name
alpha_thumbnail

Type
boolean

default false

Description
When set to `true`, the task additionally renders a transparent-background (RGBA) version of the preview and returns it as `alpha_thumbnail_url` on the GET response. The existing `thumbnail_url` field is unchanged.

### Returns

The `result` property of the response contains the task `id` of the newly created Retexture task.

### Failure Modes

-

Name
`400 - Bad Request`

Description
The request was unacceptable. Common causes:

  * **Missing parameter**: Either `model_url` or `input_task_id` must be provided.
  * **Missing style**: Either `text_style_prompt` or `image_style_url` must be provided.
  * **Invalid input task**: The `input_task_id` must refer to a successful task from a supported model.
  * **Invalid model format**: The `model_url` points to a file with an unsupported extension.
  * **Unreachable URL**: The `model_url` or `image_style_url` could not be downloaded.

-

Name
`401 - Unauthorized`

Description
Authentication failed. Please check your API key.

-

Name
`402 - Payment Required`

Description
Insufficient credits to perform this task.

-

Name
`429 - Too Many Requests`

Description
You have exceeded your rate limit.

### Request

cURL

JavaScript

Python

POST

/openapi/v1/retexture

```bash
# Retexture with text prompt
curl https://api.meshy.ai/openapi/v1/retexture \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${YOUR_API_KEY}" \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d '{
    "model_url": "https://cdn.meshy.ai/model/example_model_2.glb",
    "text_style_prompt": "red fangs, Samurai outfit that fused with japanese batik style",
    "enable_original_uv": true,
    "enable_pbr": true
  }'

# Retexture with image style and PBR
curl https://api.meshy.ai/openapi/v1/retexture \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${YOUR_API_KEY}" \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d '{
    "model_url": "https://cdn.meshy.ai/model/example_model_2.glb",
    "image_style_url": "https://cdn.meshy.ai/image/example_image.jpg",
    "ai_model": "latest",
    "enable_pbr": true,
    "enable_original_uv": true
  }'

```CopyCopied!

## [Stream a Retexture Task](#stream-a-retexture-task)

This endpoint streams real-time updates for a Retexture task using Server-Sent Events (SSE).

For `PENDING` or `IN_PROGRESS` tasks, the response stream will only include necessary `progress` and `status` fields.

## [The Retexture Task Object](#the-retexture-task-object)

The Retexture Task object is a work unit that Meshy uses to generate a 3D texture from a either text or image inputs.
The model has the following properties:

### Properties

-

Name
id

Type
string

Description
Unique identifier for the task. While we use a k-sortable UUID for task ids as the
implementation detail, you should **not** make any assumptions about the format of the id.

-

Name
type

Type
string

Description
Type of the Retexture task. The value is `retexture`.

-

Name
model_urls

Type
object

Description
Downloadable URL to the textured 3D model file generated by Meshy.


  *

Name
`glb`

Type
string

Description
Downloadable URL to the GLB file.

  *

Name
`fbx`

Type
string

Description
Downloadable URL to the FBX file.

  *

Name
`obj`

Type
string

Description
Downloadable URL to the OBJ file.

  *

Name
`usdz`

Type
string

Description
Downloadable URL to the USDZ file.

  *

Name
`mtl`

Type
string

Description
Downloadable URL to the MTL file, returned alongside OBJ exports when textures are present.

  *

Name
`stl`

Type
string

Description
Downloadable URL to the STL file.

  *

Name
`3mf`

Type
string

Description
Downloadable URL to the 3MF file. Only present when `3mf` was requested via `target_formats`.

-

Name
text_style_prompt

Type
string

Description
This is the text prompt that was used to create the texturing task.

-

Name
image_style_url

Type
string

Description
This is the image input that was used to create the texturing task.

-

Name
thumbnail_url

Type
string

Description
Downloadable URL to the thumbnail image of the model file.

-

Name
alpha_thumbnail_url

Type
string

Description
Downloadable URL to a transparent-background (RGBA) version of `thumbnail_url`. Only present when the task was created with `alpha_thumbnail: true` and the transparent preview was successfully rendered; otherwise this field is omitted.

-

Name
progress

Type
integer

Description
Progress of the task. If the task is not started yet, this property will be `0`. Once the task has succeeded, this will become `100`.

-

Name
started_at

Type
timestamp

Description
Timestamp of when the task was started, in milliseconds. If the task is not started yet, this property will be `0`.

  
      A timestamp represents the number of milliseconds elapsed since January 1, 1970 UTC, following
the [RFC 3339](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc3339) standard.
For example, Friday, September 1, 2023 12:00:00 PM GMT is represented as `1693569600000`. This applies
to **all** timestamps in Meshy API.

-

Name
created_at

Type
timestamp

Description
Timestamp of when the task was created, in milliseconds.

-

Name
expires_at

Type
timestamp

Description
Timestamp of when the task result expires, in milliseconds.

-

Name
finished_at

Type
timestamp

Description
Timestamp of when the task was finished, in milliseconds. If the task is not finished yet, this property will be `0`.

-

Name
status

Type
string

Description
Status of the task. Possible values are one of `PENDING`, `IN_PROGRESS`, `SUCCEEDED`, `FAILED`, `CANCELED`.

-

Name
texture_urls

Type
array

Description
An array of texture URL objects that are generated from the task. Normally this only contains **one** texture URL object. Each texture URL has the following properties:


  *

Name
`base_color`

Type
string

Description
Downloadable URL to the base color map image.

  *

Name
`metallic`

Type
string

Description
Downloadable URL to the metallic map image.

  
            If the task is created with `enable_pbr: false`, this property will be omitted.

  *

Name
`normal`

Type
string

Description
Downloadable URL to the normal map image.

  
            If the task is created with `enable_pbr: false`, this property will be omitted.

  *

Name
`roughness`

Type
string

Description
Downloadable URL to the roughness map image.

  
            If the task is created with `enable_pbr: false`, this property will be omitted.

  *

Name
`emission`

Type
string

Description
Downloadable URL to the emission map image.

  
            If the task is created with `enable_pbr: false`, or `ai_model` is `meshy-5`, this property will be omitted.

-

Name
preceding_tasks

Type
integer

Description
The count of preceding tasks.

  
      This property only presents when the task status is `PENDING`.

-

Name
task_error

Type
object

Description
Error details for failed tasks. See [Errors](https://docs.meshy.ai/en/api/errors#task-errors) for the full `task_error` object reference.

-

Name
consumed_credits

Type
integer

Description
The number of credits consumed by this task. Present when the task status is `PENDING`, `IN_PROGRESS`, or `SUCCEEDED`. Returns `0` for `FAILED` tasks (credits are refunded on failure).

# How to Use Texture Edit

Guide to using the Texture Edit feature in Meshy to modify and refine your 3D model textures.

 Updated over a week ago

Our **Texture Edit** tool lets you customize the look of 3D models you've already generated. You can change colors, add patterns, or apply entirely new textures to specific parts of your model.



# 1. Navigating to Texture Edit

Once you've generated a 3D model, you'll see a **Texture Edit** icon on the bottom middle section of your screen:



[![](https://downloads.intercomcdn.com/i/o/ipvgg8in/1654142126/a3753301a0081d83d1bb521566d2/Screenshot+2025-08-04+at+11_11_26%E2%80%AFPM.png?expires=1779343200&signature=1d361492013b7928ce2fc0a1a28deca6a1c03a56ef3c8c148c583d868af8e79d&req=dSYiEsh6n4BdX%2FMW1HO4zSB6kowWidZzbKYL3Q0KWJhdSg%2BTe5iCSlGh8dVx%0AKtI3EGNtruQURhFE67k%3D%0A)](https://downloads.intercomcdn.com/i/o/ipvgg8in/1654142126/a3753301a0081d83d1bb521566d2/Screenshot+2025-08-04+at+11_11_26%E2%80%AFPM.png?expires=1779343200&signature=1d361492013b7928ce2fc0a1a28deca6a1c03a56ef3c8c148c583d868af8e79d&req=dSYiEsh6n4BdX%2FMW1HO4zSB6kowWidZzbKYL3Q0KWJhdSg%2BTe5iCSlGh8dVx%0AKtI3EGNtruQURhFE67k%3D%0A)



By default, you will be in Free Camera Mode, with the left part of your screen showing your model and history of edits once you make them:



[![](https://downloads.intercomcdn.com/i/o/ipvgg8in/1654148328/db0b1ab30cbc6d62c7c903521916/Screenshot+2025-08-04+at+11_19_19%E2%80%AFPM.png?expires=1779343200&signature=4e15f4c647f4ba87cb0780cc5f8de2d816b1a9ea6a47e3a25aa7522e25e0c382&req=dSYiEsh6lYJdUfMW1HO4zVjGDdDrjFacdSWLhxWTeSyghkv%2FwLoJwrjI58T0%0ApZqd0Rc8%2FTZSpylu024%3D%0A)](https://downloads.intercomcdn.com/i/o/ipvgg8in/1654148328/db0b1ab30cbc6d62c7c903521916/Screenshot+2025-08-04+at+11_19_19%E2%80%AFPM.png?expires=1779343200&signature=4e15f4c647f4ba87cb0780cc5f8de2d816b1a9ea6a47e3a25aa7522e25e0c382&req=dSYiEsh6lYJdUfMW1HO4zVjGDdDrjFacdSWLhxWTeSyghkv%2FwLoJwrjI58T0%0ApZqd0Rc8%2FTZSpylu024%3D%0A)



Please note: the original texture will be shown in this window, and not the PBR preview if you had that selected previously.



## 2. Selecting Your Mesh

Before you can edit, you need to select the part of the model you want to change.

- **Click** on a specific part of your 3D model. For example, if you have a model of a knight, you can select just the helmet, the sword, or the shield.

- Once selected, the chosen area will be highlighted with a light green outline:

[![](https://downloads.intercomcdn.com/i/o/ipvgg8in/1654151400/ed9bc5e1edfd878b6c09c5cf60ae/Screenshot+2025-08-04+at+11_22_46%E2%80%AFPM.png?expires=1779343200&signature=1ed1dcea53895dad2cd635647c2533568334f52491a5b5d7d84d179ddfe7e7a2&req=dSYiEsh7nIVfWfMW1HO4zdeSQ%2BGk4NWMtR1UpGwbSC0xbkD9QskCBy%2BjTEWV%0A6yFzEjAqJNCv8hlgDkY%3D%0A)](https://downloads.intercomcdn.com/i/o/ipvgg8in/1654151400/ed9bc5e1edfd878b6c09c5cf60ae/Screenshot+2025-08-04+at+11_22_46%E2%80%AFPM.png?expires=1779343200&signature=1ed1dcea53895dad2cd635647c2533568334f52491a5b5d7d84d179ddfe7e7a2&req=dSYiEsh7nIVfWfMW1HO4zdeSQ%2BGk4NWMtR1UpGwbSC0xbkD9QskCBy%2BjTEWV%0A6yFzEjAqJNCv8hlgDkY%3D%0A)



- You use either a brush or lasso tool, and select the size of the brush. There is also an erase button, a toggle on/off selection button, and trash icon to delete your selection:

  

  [![](https://downloads.intercomcdn.com/i/o/ipvgg8in/1654152632/f0da56cc68ecc1929a630836b778/Screenshot+2025-08-04+at+11_23_08%E2%80%AFPM.png?expires=1779343200&signature=dcb86655a10f2ce5e97d5273d8972dbbed921573e4076b6aa7cb9225fc111d14&req=dSYiEsh7n4dcW%2FMW1HO4zaGP6ruLtRoD7kwomS015%2BbokVcuK7AGF0OIuSr8%0AW8%2Fd%0A)](https://downloads.intercomcdn.com/i/o/ipvgg8in/1654152632/f0da56cc68ecc1929a630836b778/Screenshot+2025-08-04+at+11_23_08%E2%80%AFPM.png?expires=1779343200&signature=dcb86655a10f2ce5e97d5273d8972dbbed921573e4076b6aa7cb9225fc111d14&req=dSYiEsh7n4dcW%2FMW1HO4zaGP6ruLtRoD7kwomS015%2BbokVcuK7AGF0OIuSr8%0AW8%2Fd%0A)
  

## 3. Writing Your Prompt

Now it's time to describe the new texture you want. In the prompt box, type a clear description of the new look:



[![](https://downloads.intercomcdn.com/i/o/ipvgg8in/1654159442/063b32de1ffef0821242d000905f/Screenshot+2025-08-04+at+11_32_25%E2%80%AFPM.png?expires=1779343200&signature=85484fa604b399ede80ab622dcbd94bb54e79bb52964c95a36c1645bd6ea647e&req=dSYiEsh7lIVbW%2FMW1HO4zarGbP51WGXiLjgBvpa7zBDmcFiyToL%2Bot%2BnpUbk%0APwuexYRzSTdXfkpQgpg%3D%0A)](https://downloads.intercomcdn.com/i/o/ipvgg8in/1654159442/063b32de1ffef0821242d000905f/Screenshot+2025-08-04+at+11_32_25%E2%80%AFPM.png?expires=1779343200&signature=85484fa604b399ede80ab622dcbd94bb54e79bb52964c95a36c1645bd6ea647e&req=dSYiEsh7lIVbW%2FMW1HO4zarGbP51WGXiLjgBvpa7zBDmcFiyToL%2Bot%2BnpUbk%0APwuexYRzSTdXfkpQgpg%3D%0A)



- **Be specific:** Instead of "change to a different texture," try "a shiny, bronze texture with intricate carvings."

- **Use descriptive words:** Mention colors, materials, and styles. For example, "a vibrant red, velvety material," or "a weathered wooden texture with visible grain."

- **Examples:**


  * `A smooth, dark-blue, metallic texture`

  * `A rustic leather texture with small stitches`

  * `A vibrant, cartoonish flame pattern`

- You can important your original text prompt, and add/edit from there.

- The **Prompt Influence Strength** allows you to control how much of an impact your prompt will have on the final texture result. Higher values will create a stronger effect, while lower values will not enhance the texture selection as much.



## 4. Generating the New Texture

After you've written your prompt, click the **Retexture** button:



[![](https://downloads.intercomcdn.com/i/o/ipvgg8in/1654163460/573e049c7826726c6804d64829b5/Screenshot+2025-08-04+at+11_37_16%E2%80%AFPM.png?expires=1779343200&signature=e398fee082ca934c386a1d1ce29782da649f670dc1866b1c142aee72ad302384&req=dSYiEsh4noVZWfMW1HO4zf%2FJYWZUB%2FiWvWp8lQFiItgxCBNO4i%2FINs1rwfvh%0AyglMlqEasoGbAuCkjJE%3D%0A)](https://downloads.intercomcdn.com/i/o/ipvgg8in/1654163460/573e049c7826726c6804d64829b5/Screenshot+2025-08-04+at+11_37_16%E2%80%AFPM.png?expires=1779343200&signature=e398fee082ca934c386a1d1ce29782da649f670dc1866b1c142aee72ad302384&req=dSYiEsh4noVZWfMW1HO4zf%2FJYWZUB%2FiWvWp8lQFiItgxCBNO4i%2FINs1rwfvh%0AyglMlqEasoGbAuCkjJE%3D%0A)



Meshy will then create a new texture and apply it to the selected part of your model. This may take a few moments.



## 5. Applying or Discarding the New Texture

You'll receive three versions of the texture, which you can choose from on the left side of your screen:



[![](https://downloads.intercomcdn.com/i/o/ipvgg8in/1654167089/1fd8dd57105f5c4c0d7724170ec4/Screenshot+2025-08-04+at+11_38_28%E2%80%AFPM.png?expires=1779343200&signature=548d0abf01d6e1dc37e45c03cfeac400b3f30a83437eb7b6f146cacb1c1f6d16&req=dSYiEsh4moFXUPMW1HO4zf7tBjJtAe%2BPzZ%2B9i%2F%2B%2FplLrhiveNWOJFrqtdxPJ%0Ac0o3MJsQ7xA0q2SD4mI%3D%0A)](https://downloads.intercomcdn.com/i/o/ipvgg8in/1654167089/1fd8dd57105f5c4c0d7724170ec4/Screenshot+2025-08-04+at+11_38_28%E2%80%AFPM.png?expires=1779343200&signature=548d0abf01d6e1dc37e45c03cfeac400b3f30a83437eb7b6f146cacb1c1f6d16&req=dSYiEsh4moFXUPMW1HO4zf7tBjJtAe%2BPzZ%2B9i%2F%2B%2FplLrhiveNWOJFrqtdxPJ%0Ac0o3MJsQ7xA0q2SD4mI%3D%0A)



- Clicking each one will show a preview of the texture on your model, on the right side of the screen.

- **Apply:** If you like the new texture, click **Apply** to save the changes to your 3D model.

- **Discard:** If it's not what you were looking for, click the trash can icon and try writing a new prompt.

## 6. How to use Brush Tools

Under this icon, there are three brush tools you can use:  
​

[![](https://downloads.intercomcdn.com/i/o/ipvgg8in/1823663354/0a81ee5d2bd8be2e077b60311b01/Screenshot+2025-11-10+at+10_20_57%E2%80%AFPM.png?expires=1779343200&signature=d5f01fa46037f6bfda4a0824fb2b0d1ac32071c2c46df07d1f5b951c53669252&req=dSglFc94noJaXfMW1HO4zYluPHijeC058gtV5st90hETnWGsy4OO1%2F3QqHzo%0AiJACWso1wEbxKyhCFF4%3D%0A)](https://downloads.intercomcdn.com/i/o/ipvgg8in/1823663354/0a81ee5d2bd8be2e077b60311b01/Screenshot+2025-11-10+at+10_20_57%E2%80%AFPM.png?expires=1779343200&signature=d5f01fa46037f6bfda4a0824fb2b0d1ac32071c2c46df07d1f5b951c53669252&req=dSglFc94noJaXfMW1HO4zYluPHijeC058gtV5st90hETnWGsy4OO1%2F3QqHzo%0AiJACWso1wEbxKyhCFF4%3D%0A)



- Healing Tool - will use the surrounding colors and patterns to heal any spot that you brush over.

- Stamp Tool - hold Ctrl/Command, and click on the spot that you want to replicate with using the brush tool. Then, click and drag on your texture to paste the cloned area.

- Solid Paint Tool - select any color from the color menu, and paint over your texture. Blur can be added as well.



## 7. Saving Your Final Model

Once you're happy with all your changes, click the **Save** **to Model** button to create a new model of your newly textured 3D model. This will not replace the original model in your collection.

# Best practices

Copy page



Master prompting for Eleven Music to achieve maximum musicality and control.

This guide summarizes the most effective techniques for prompting the Eleven Music model. It covers genre & creativity, instrument & vocal isolation, musical control, and structural timing & lyrics.

The model is designed to understand intent and generate complete, context-aware audio based on your goals. High-level prompts like *“ad for a sneaker brand”* or *“peaceful meditation with voiceover”* are often enough to guide the model toward tone, structure, and content that match your use case.

## Genre & Creativity

The model demonstrates strong adherence to genre conventions and emotional tone. Both musical descriptors of emotional tone and tone descriptors themselves will work. It responds effectively to both:

- Abstract mood descriptors (e.g., “eerie,” “foreboding”)
- Detailed musical language (e.g., “dissonant violin screeches over a pulsing sub-bass”)


Prompt length and detail do not always correlate with better quality outputs. For more creative and unexpected results, try using simple, evocative keywords to let the model interpret and compose freely.

## Instrument & Vocal Isolation

The v1 model does not generate stems directly from a full track. To create stems with greater control, use targeted prompts and structure:

- Use the word “solo” before instruments (e.g., “solo electric guitar,” “solo piano in C minor”).
- For vocals, use “a cappella” before the vocal description (e.g., “a cappella female vocals,” “a cappella male chorus”).


To improve stem quality and control:

- Include key, tempo (BPM), and musical tone (e.g., “a cappella vocals in A major, 90 BPM, soulful and raw”).
- Be as musically descriptive as possible to guide the model’s output.


## Musical Control

The model accurately follows BPM and often captures the intended musical key. To gain more control over timing and harmony, include tempo cues like “130 BPM” and key signatures like “in A minor” in your prompt.

To influence vocal delivery and tone, use expressive descriptors such as “raw,” “live,” “glitching,” “breathy,” or “aggressive.”

The model can effectively render multiple vocalists, use prompts like “two singers harmonizing in C” to direct vocal arrangement.

In general, more detailed prompts lead to greater control and expressiveness in the output.

## Structural Timing & Lyrics

You can specify the length of the song (e.g., “60 seconds”) or use auto mode to let the model determine the duration. If lyrics are not provided, the model will generate structured lyrics that match the chosen or auto-detected length.

By default, most music prompts will include lyrics. To generate music without vocals, add “instrumental only” to your prompt. You can also write your own lyrics for more creative control. The model uses your lyrics in combination with the prompt length to determine vocal structure and placement.

To manage when vocals begin or end, include clear timing cues like:

- “lyrics begin at 15 seconds”
- “instrumental only after 1:45”


The model supports multilingual lyric generation. To change the language of a generated song in our UI, use follow-ups like “make it Japanese” or “translate to Spanish.”

## Sample Prompts

The model allows you to move beyond song descriptors and into intent for maximum creativity.

###### Video Game with Musical Control

###### Mascara Audio Ad Creative

###### Live Indie Rock Performance

```
| Create an intense, fast-paced electronic track for a high-adrenaline video game scene.    |
| ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Use driving synth arpeggios, punchy drums, distorted bass, glitch effects, and            |
| aggressive rhythmic textures. The tempo should be fast, 130–150 bpm, with rising tension, |
| quick transitions, and dynamic energy bursts.                                             |


```


## Advanced: Composition plans

For precise control over section structure, lyrics placement, and multi-vocalist arrangements, use composition plans instead of simple text prompts.

[Composition plans guideLearn how to structure songs with sections, global/local styles, and proper lyrics formatting for maximum control.](https://elevenlabs.io/docs/eleven-api/guides/how-to/music/composition-plans)

# Meshy PBR re-export spec — Little SuperClaws AR figures

**Goal:** Re-export the 5 existing "Little SuperClaws" characters with full PBR texture sets so they read as properly lit, tactile clay figures in iPhone AR Quick Look (USDZ), instead of the current flat, albedo-only look.

**Characters:** Clawd (blue), Nessa (red), Deirdre (green), Decklan (yellow), Gerald (purple).

**Current state:** Each GLB ships a single baked base-color (albedo) texture only. Under AR Quick Look's image-based environment lighting the surface has no normal/roughness/metallic data, so it looks uniformly flat and plasticky.

**Good news from research:** Meshy can re-texture the *existing* meshes (no regeneration needed) and emit a full PBR set. See "What the research confirmed" at the bottom.

---

## 1. Why PBR maps matter for AR Quick Look

AR Quick Look shades surfaces with `UsdPreviewSurface`, which is a physically based shader driven by an image-based environment light. It reads `diffuseColor` (albedo), plus `normal`, `roughness`, `metallic`, and `occlusion` inputs. With only an albedo map, every pixel returns the same roughness/metallic/normal defaults, so the environment light hits the whole figure identically and it reads flat — no surface microdetail, no soft self-shadowing, no material variation. Adding normal (fakes surface relief), roughness (controls how sharp/soft the reflection is), metallic (here: zero, so it stays dielectric/clay), and AO (darkens crevices) is what makes the figure look lit and tactile.

---

## 2. Meshy steps and settings (per character)

Use Meshy's **Retexture** feature (Web app: "Texture" / Retexture; API: `POST /openapi/v1/retexture`). Retexture applies new PBR maps to an *existing* mesh — the 5 models do **not** need to be regenerated.

**Settings to use:**

| Setting | Value | Why |
|---|---|---|
| Input | The existing per-character GLB (`model_url` or `input_task_id`) | Re-texture in place, keep the mesh |
| `enable_pbr` | `true` | **Required** — this is what produces metallic + roughness + normal maps |
| `enable_original_uv` | `true` | Preserve the model's existing UVs so the new maps line up with the current art |
| `ai_model` | `latest` (Meshy 6) | Needed for `remove_lighting`; also enables 4K base color if ever wanted |
| `hd_texture` | `false` | 2K base color is plenty for a ~2cm AR figure (see note) |
| `remove_lighting` | `true` | Strips baked highlights/shadows from albedo so AR's own lighting does the work — critical, otherwise lighting is double-baked and looks flat/dirty |
| `text_style_prompt` | Per character, e.g. *"matte clay figurine, smooth vinyl-toy surface, soft non-reflective finish, [colour] body"* | Drives a clay/matte aesthetic |
| `target_formats` | `["glb","usdz"]` | Only generate what we need; faster |

**Resolution:** 2K (2048×2048) is the right call. PBR maps in Meshy are **always 2K** regardless of settings, and base color defaults to 2K. A figure rendered at ~2cm in AR never resolves more than 2K of texel detail, so 4K base color (`hd_texture: true`) is wasted bytes and a heavier USDZ. Keep it at 2K.

**Clay/matte aesthetic (high roughness, zero metallic):** Meshy's generated roughness/metallic come from the prompt, so they may not be perfectly matte. To guarantee the clay look, after export **override the material constants** rather than trusting the generated maps:
- **metallic = 0.0** (flat scalar, no metallic map needed — clay is a dielectric).
- **roughness ≈ 0.7–0.85** (high, matte). Either use Meshy's roughness map, or if it reads too glossy, replace it with a flat ~0.8 scalar.
- Keep the **normal** and **AO** maps — those add the tactile detail and are the whole point.

If a character still reads glossy in AR, the fix is almost always: drop a flat high-roughness value and zero metallic.

---

## 3. What to hand back (deliverables)

Preferred, in priority order:

1. **GLB with embedded maps (preferred).** One GLB per character with base color + normal + roughness + metallic + AO packed inside. Meshy's GLB export carries the full PBR set, so this is the cleanest handoff. Verify the GLB actually contains 5 textures (not just 1) before sending — confirms PBR survived export.
2. **USDZ per character (bonus).** Meshy also exports USDZ directly with PBR; include it if available so it can be sanity-checked in AR Quick Look immediately.
3. **Fallback: a folder of PNG maps per character**, if the GLB doesn't embed cleanly. Naming convention (one folder per character):

```
clawd/
  clawd_base.png        # base color / albedo (sRGB)
  clawd_normal.png      # tangent-space normal (linear)
  clawd_roughness.png   # roughness (linear, grayscale)
  clawd_metallic.png    # metallic (linear, grayscale) — expect ~black/zero
  clawd_ao.png          # ambient occlusion (linear, grayscale)
```

Repeat for `nessa/`, `deirdre/`, `decklan/`, `gerald/`. All maps 2K. Flag the colour-space (base = sRGB; normal/roughness/metallic/AO = linear) so they wire up correctly.

> Note on AO: Meshy's PBR output is base_color + metallic + roughness + normal (+ emission on Meshy 6). If a discrete **AO map is not in the export**, that's fine — AO can be baked from the mesh on our side, or the `occlusion` input left to default. Don't block the handoff on AO.

---

## 4. How these wire into UsdPreviewSurface (dev context — brief)

When converting/authoring the USDZ, map each texture to the matching `UsdPreviewSurface` input:

| Meshy map | UsdPreviewSurface input | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| base color | `diffuseColor` | sRGB |
| normal | `normal` | tangent-space, linear |
| roughness | `roughness` | linear, scalar/grayscale |
| metallic | `metallic` | linear — set/override to **0.0** for clay |
| AO | `occlusion` | linear; optional, default if absent |

If exporting GLB → USDZ, Apple's `usdzconvert` / Reality Converter handles this mapping automatically from a correctly-packed glTF metallic-roughness material. The manual table above is the fallback if authoring USD by hand.

---

## 5. Paste-to-Yash handoff checklist

```
LITTLE SUPERCLAWS — PBR RE-EXPORT (Meshy Retexture)

For each of: Clawd (blue), Nessa (red), Deirdre (green), Decklan (yellow), Gerald (purple)

[ ] Run Meshy RETEXTURE on the existing GLB (do NOT regenerate the mesh)
[ ] enable_pbr = true              (generates normal + roughness + metallic)
[ ] enable_original_uv = true      (keep existing UVs so art lines up)
[ ] ai_model = latest (Meshy 6)
[ ] remove_lighting = true         (strip baked highlights — important)
[ ] hd_texture = false             (2K is plenty for a 2cm AR figure)
[ ] text_style_prompt = matte clay figurine, smooth vinyl-toy finish,
    soft non-reflective surface, [character colour] body
[ ] target_formats = ["glb","usdz"]

[ ] Force clay look: metallic = 0.0, roughness ≈ 0.7–0.85 (override if Meshy
    output reads glossy)

DELIVER per character (preferred → fallback):
[ ] GLB with embedded PBR maps  ← preferred; verify it contains ~5 textures, not 1
[ ] USDZ (if Meshy exports it) for instant AR Quick Look check
[ ] Fallback only if GLB won't embed: folder of 2K PNGs named
    base / normal / roughness / metallic / ao
[ ] Note colour space: base = sRGB; normal/roughness/metallic/ao = linear

SANITY CHECK before sending:
[ ] Open each USDZ/GLB on an iPhone in AR Quick Look
[ ] Confirm surface relief (normal) + soft matte highlights (roughness) read
[ ] Confirm it does NOT look chrome/metallic (metallic must be 0)
```

---

## What the research confirmed (Meshy, current docs)

- **Meshy exports a full PBR set.** With `enable_pbr: true`, Retexture/texture tasks return `base_color`, `metallic`, `roughness`, and `normal` maps (plus `emission` on Meshy 6 / `latest`). Without it, only base color is returned. ([Retexture API docs](https://docs.meshy.ai/en/api/retexture))
- **Existing models can be re-textured — no regeneration.** Retexture accepts an existing mesh via `model_url` (`.glb`, `.gltf`, `.obj`, `.fbx`, `.stl`) or `input_task_id`, and `enable_original_uv: true` preserves the current UVs/art. ([Retexture API docs](https://docs.meshy.ai/en/api/retexture))
- **Resolution:** PBR maps are **always 2K**; base color is 2K by default and can go to 4K only via `hd_texture: true` on Meshy 6. 2K is the right choice here. ([Retexture API docs](https://docs.meshy.ai/en/api/retexture))
- **GLB packs the maps; USDZ is a native export target.** Meshy outputs GLB, FBX, OBJ, USDZ, STL, 3MF; GLB is the recommended format for PBR fidelity (OBJ+MTL doesn't carry PBR), and USDZ is exported directly — ideal for AR Quick Look. ([Retexture API docs](https://docs.meshy.ai/en/api/retexture), [Meshy AI Texture Generator](https://www.meshy.ai/features/ai-texture-generator))
- **AO caveat:** Meshy's documented PBR output does not list a standalone ambient-occlusion map (it's base/metallic/roughness/normal/emission). AO can be baked on our side or left to the `occlusion` default; don't block on it.

**Sources:**
- [Retexture API — Meshy Docs](https://docs.meshy.ai/en/api/retexture)
- [How to Use Texture Edit — Meshy Help Center](https://help.meshy.ai/en/articles/11936711-how-to-use-texture-edit)
- [AI Texture Generator — Meshy](https://www.meshy.ai/features/ai-texture-generator)
