# Little SuperClaws — audio layer plan (ElevenLabs)

Audio plan for the Little SuperClaws shorts: 5 stylized claymation AR heroes (Clawd — blue, anxious leader; Nessa — red, hot-headed muscle; Deirdre — green, cool strategist; Decklan — yellow, showboat; Gerald — purple, nervous) filmed as 2cm figures in real environments doing walk cycles, dances, and poses. Goal: a short funny theme "in our style" plus tightly-scoped sound effects mapped to specific animations. Everything below is ready to paste into ElevenLabs tonight — no API connection required.

Researched against elevenlabs.io/docs (Music + Sound Effects), current as of June 2026.

---

## 1. Feasibility summary

Short answer: **yes to both.** ElevenLabs has two separate products that cover exactly what you need, and both are usable tonight in the browser at elevenlabs.io with no setup beyond a paid plan.

| Capability | Product | Can it do it? | Length | Output format | API? |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Funny superhero theme | **Eleven Music** | Yes — text-prompt music in any style, instrumental or with vocals | 3 sec – 5 min (you'll use ~15–30s) | MP3 (44.1kHz, 128–192kbps) and WAV | Yes — `POST /v1/music`, paid plans |
| Movement / animation SFX | **Sound Effects** (text-to-sound) | Yes — text-to-SFX, simple effects and multi-step sequences | 0.5 – 30 sec per generation | MP3 for all; WAV at 48kHz for non-looping; seamless loop option | Yes — `POST /v1/sound-generation` |

Key facts that matter for this project:
- **Music** is prompt-driven (up to 4,100 characters). You can set exact length in the UI or via `music_length_ms`. Add **"instrumental only"** to kill the default vocals — you want this for a theme sting. Current model is Music v2 in the UI (v1 default on API during transition). Cleared for commercial use including social media and film/TV.
- **Sound Effects** takes a plain text prompt (`text`), optional `duration_seconds` (0.5–30, or auto), a `loop` flag for seamless loops (v2 model), and `prompt_influence` (0–1, default 0.3 — raise it toward 0.5–0.7 to make it hug the prompt more tightly and stay consistent across re-rolls).
- Both let you **re-generate** for variations and pick the best take. Budget 2–4 generations per item; not every roll lands.
- One gap to know: AI music **stems** aren't separated from a finished track on v1. If you want isolated layers (e.g., just the toy drums), prompt them separately with the word "solo" rather than expecting to split a finished mix.

---

## 2. Theme music — ready-to-paste Eleven Music prompts

Target: a ~15–30 second comedic claymation-superhero theme. Brass + toy percussion, wonky charm, heroic-but-tiny, ends on a clean button so it can also work as a logo sting. All four are **instrumental** (add lyrics later only if you want a sung "Little Super-Claws!" tag).

Tips before you paste:
- Set length to **20 seconds** (or 15s for a tight sting, 30s for an intro with room to breathe).
- Keep "instrumental only" in the prompt.
- Generate each variant 2–3 times and keep the take with the cleanest ending — you want a hard stop you can cut to a "ta-da" pose.

**Variant A — the toy-band hero march (the safe default)**
```
A short, comedic superhero theme for a stop-motion claymation cartoon about tiny clay heroes. Playful and slightly absurd, NOT epic or serious. Bouncy toy-band march at around 120 BPM: parping muted trumpet and tuba doing a heroic fanfare, plinky toy xylophone, hand-claps, woodblock and tiny tambourine, a comedic bassoon countermelody. Wonky, charming, a little out of tune on purpose. Builds to a triumphant little fanfare and ends on a clean "ta-da" button. Instrumental only.
```

**Variant B — brass-forward, more swagger (for Decklan/Nessa energy)**
```
A 20-second goofy superhero fanfare in a quirky stop-motion style. Big cartoonish brass section — trumpets and trombone slides, a fat tuba oompah bassline — over a marching snare, kazoo, and clattery toy percussion. Mischievous, jaunty, comedic timing with little stumbles and a slide-whistle accent. Heroic but knee-high, like a tiny band marching across a kitchen table. Tight ending on a brass stab. Instrumental only.
```

**Variant C — anxious-but-determined (leans into Clawd/Gerald)**
```
A short, funny theme for a stop-motion claymation superhero who is brave but nervous. Tip-toeing pizzicato strings and a wobbly clarinet melody that keeps almost-tripping, light brass swells that try to be heroic, plucky ukulele, soft mallet percussion, and a gentle comedic timpani roll. Whimsical, slightly absurd, charmingly clumsy, building courage toward a small triumphant finish. Around 110 BPM. Ends on a clean resolved chord. Instrumental only.
```

**Variant D — vintage cartoon / Tom-and-Jerry-meets-claymation (most "characterful")**
```
A 15-second comedic superhero sting in a vintage cartoon orchestra style, reimagined for tiny claymation figures. Mickey-Mousing comedic orchestration: muted brass fanfare, walking pizzicato bass, xylophone runs, slide whistle, plunger-muted trumpet "wah-wah", brushed snare and tambourine. Bright, bouncy, mischievous and absurd, with exaggerated comic timing. Heroic mini-fanfare that lands on a clean final stinger. Instrumental only.
```

How to use them: generate A first as your baseline. If it reads too "real band," go to D for more cartoon character; if you want more macho swagger, go to B. Keep two finished takes — a **full ~20s intro** and a **3–5s button** (re-prompt one of these at 5 seconds for a stinger you can drop on a hero pose).

---

## 3. Sound effects — the essential ~8 (with paste-ready prompts)

You're right that there are too many possible SFX. The trick for tiny clay figures is that **every sound should feel small, soft, and slightly squishy** — clay, felt, plastic, not real boots and metal. The table below is the high-value short list. Generate each at the listed duration, keep `prompt_influence` around 0.5, and re-roll 2–3 times.

| # | Animation / moment | Why it matters | Duration | Ready-to-paste Sound Effects prompt | Loop? |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | **Walk cycle** | Used constantly; sells the figure as alive | 2–3s | `Tiny soft clay footsteps, small squishy plasticine steps on a hard surface, light rhythmic squelchy pat-pat-pat, gentle and cute, no reverb` | Make a 3s seamless loop |
| 2 | **Idle bounce / breathing** | Fills "doing nothing" shots so they don't feel dead | 2–3s | `Soft springy rubbery bounce, gentle squishy clay wobble, light boing, small and cute, subtle, repeating` | Yes, seamless loop |
| 3 | **Jump up** | Pairs with #4 for any hop | 0.7s | `A small cartoonish boing jump, soft springy clay launch, light squishy whoosh upward, cute and quick` | No (one-shot) |
| 4 | **Land / plop** | The comedic payoff of a jump | 0.7s | `A tiny soft clay plop landing, small squishy thud, gentle rubbery impact with a little settle wobble, cute, no reverb` | No (one-shot) |
| 5 | **Claw snap / signature move** | Brand sound — the "SuperClaws" signature | 0.8s | `A quick cartoonish claw snap, small plastic-rubbery click-clack pinch, snappy and crisp with a tiny comedic sproing tail, cute` | No (one-shot) |
| 6 | **"Ta-da" hero pose** | Punctuates the end of an animation or the theme | 1.5s | `A short comedic ta-da pose accent, tiny triumphant toy fanfare stab with a little sparkle shimmer and a soft cymbal tap, cute and proud` | No (one-shot) |
| 7 | **Whoosh entrance / exit** | Hero swoops into or out of frame | 0.8s | `A small fast cartoon whoosh, light airy swish of a tiny figure zipping past, soft and playful, quick` | No (one-shot) |
| 8 | **Dance groove** | Backs any dance animation; can sit under music | 4–6s | `Bouncy playful toy percussion groove, plinky xylophone and woodblock with light hand-claps and tiny tambourine, cute clay-cartoon dance rhythm, around 120 BPM, looping` | Yes, seamless loop |

**What to skip or fake (so you don't drown in files):**
- **Per-character variants** — don't generate 5 different walk cycles. Make one walk loop and **pitch it** in the editor (Nessa lower/heavier, Gerald higher/lighter). Same for the idle bounce.
- **Whoosh AND jump AND land as separate things on every hop** — most hops only need jump (#3) + land (#4). Reserve the whoosh (#7) for actual entrances/exits.
- **Ambient room tone, fabric rustle, prop foley, dialogue blips, UI/comic "pow" graphics** — nice-to-haves, not now. Add them only if a specific shot begs for it.
- **A unique SFX per dance** — one dance groove loop (#8) covers all of them; trim to length.

That's it: 8 generations, 3 of which loop, and you have a kit that covers walk, idle, jump, land, signature move, pose, entrance, and dance. Re-roll the few that don't land rather than expanding the list.

---

## 4. Workflow — generate, drop in, sync to beats

1. **Generate (tonight, in browser).** Open elevenlabs.io. In **Eleven Music**, paste theme variants A–D, set 20s + instrumental, keep the best 1–2 takes; download WAV. In **Sound Effects**, paste the 8 prompts above, set durations, toggle **Loop** on #1/#2/#8, download. Name files clearly: `theme_A_20s.wav`, `sfx_walk_loop.wav`, `sfx_clawsnap.wav`, etc. Keep an "alts" folder for second-best takes.
2. **Drop into your editor.** You already have the **video-editor skill** available here — use it to assemble the timeline: footage on the picture track, theme music on one audio track, SFX on a second.
3. **Sync to animation beats.** Place the figure footage first, then drag each one-shot to its frame: claw-snap on the snap frame, plop on the contact frame of a landing, ta-da on the held pose. For loops (walk, idle, dance), stretch the loop across the animation's duration and trim at a clean zero-crossing.
4. **Pitch/vary per character in the editor, not in ElevenLabs.** Shift the shared walk/idle/bounce loops a few semitones per hero so all five feel distinct from one source file.
5. **Mix.** Music sits ~6–10 dB under the SFX during action beats; duck the music slightly when the claw-snap or ta-da hits so the gag lands. Keep the theme button (the hard ending) aligned to the final hero pose.

Practical tip: AI-generated one-shots often have a tiny silent lead-in — trim that head so the sound hits exactly on the frame, otherwise everything feels a few frames late.

---

## 5. If you connect the ElevenLabs API later

Everything above is manual-but-fast. Connecting the ElevenLabs API (it exists for both products on paid plans — `POST /v1/music` and `POST /v1/sound-generation`) would let this agent automate the tedious parts:

- **Batch-generate the whole SFX kit in one go** from a list of prompts, including the loop flag and exact durations, and drop named files straight into your project folder — no clicking through the UI 8+ times.
- **Auto-generate per-character pitch variants** and alt takes, then let you pick.
- **Re-roll on command** ("give me 3 more claw-snaps, snappier") and save only the keepers.
- **Tie generation to the edit**: e.g., read your animation beat list and produce a matched SFX for each moment at the right length.
- **Regenerate the theme at multiple lengths** (5s sting / 15s / 30s) from one prompt automatically.

Until then, the prompts in sections 2 and 3 are built to be pasted as-is. Connecting the API only changes *how fast* you produce the kit, not *what's possible* — you can ship the whole audio layer tonight without it.

input.content:
# Little SuperClaws — Meshy rigging + animation spec

Execution-ready spec for rigging and animating the five Little SuperClaws characters in Meshy AI, then exporting rigged GLBs with walk + dance + idle clips for the iPhone AR Quick Look (USDZ) and web `model-viewer` pipeline.

Characters: Clawd (blue), Nessa (red), Deirdre (green), Decklan (yellow), Gerald (purple). Source files: single-mesh GLB, one baked albedo texture each, ~160k–320k tris.

> Critical fact to know before starting: Meshy auto-rigging only accepts **textured humanoid GLB with ≤300,000 faces**. Several of our models exceed this and need a remesh/decimate pass first. See section 5.

---

## 1. UI workflow — rigging each character

Web app: https://www.meshy.ai → **Animate** (or **Rig & Animate**) workspace.

Per character:

1. **Pre-checks before upload** (do these to maximize auto-rig success):
   - **Single connected mesh, textured.** Meshy will reject untextured meshes and non-humanoid/unclear-limb meshes. Our models are already single-mesh with a baked albedo — good.
   - **A/T-pose, limbs separated from torso.** Auto-rig does pose estimation; arms/legs must be clearly distinguishable from the body. Claws spread slightly away from the hips/thighs help; arms angled down-and-out (A-pose) or straight out (T-pose) both work. Avoid limbs fused to the torso or to each other.
   - **Facing +Z (glTF forward).** When rigging from a `model_url`/upload, the character's face must point toward +Z. Models facing another axis fail pose estimation. Confirm forward axis in Blender/three before upload.
   - **Upright, feet near origin, symmetrical.** Symmetry improves skeleton placement; left/right limbs in mirrored positions.
   - **Face count ≤ 300k.** Decimate any model over the limit first (see section 5).
2. **Upload** the GLB into the Animate workspace.
3. **Set character type / template.** Choose the **Humanoid / Biped** template. There is no separate "claws" template — claws are treated as hands. Pick Humanoid Biped for all five; the wrist/hand bones will land at the claw base (this is fine and is what we want).
4. **Set height.** Enter an approximate real-world height to scale the rig. Our figures are tiny but enter a normal humanoid height (e.g. **1.7 m**, the default) — height only affects internal rig scaling/proportion guesses, not final export size. Do **not** enter 0.02 m; that can confuse scaling. Final 2 cm sizing is handled at USDZ/model-viewer conversion.
5. **Run auto-rig.** Completes in well under a minute per model. Meshy builds the skeleton and skin weights and previews a default walk on the rigged character.
6. **Inspect the skeleton in preview.** Confirm spine, hips, shoulders, elbows, knees, and wrist/claw bones sit roughly correctly and the mesh deforms cleanly on the preview walk. If the skeleton is misplaced, see section 5.
7. **Proceed to animation** (section 2) once the rig looks correct.

Repeat for all five. Rig each character once; you can then apply many animation clips to that one rig without re-rigging.

---

## 2. Animation presets per character

Meshy exposes a named preset library (500+ clips). Each preset has a stable **`action_id`** integer (used by the API; in the UI you pick the named clip from the **Dancing / Walk & Run / Daily Actions** categories). For every character apply **one walk + one dance + one idle** at minimum. Below are concrete, fitting picks; the agent can swap within the same category to taste.

Personality cues: Clawd = anxious leader, Nessa = hot-headed muscle, Deirdre = cool strategist, Decklan = showboat, Gerald = nervous.

| Character | Walk (preset · id) | Dance (preset · id) | Idle (preset · id) |
|---|---|---|---|
| **Clawd** (blue, anxious leader) | `Thoughtful_Walk` · 121 | `OMG_Groove` · 79 | `Confused_Scratch` · 36 |
| **Nessa** (red, hot-headed muscle) | `Confident_Strut` · 107 | `Boom_Dance` · 66 | `Angry_Ground_Stomp` · 255 |
| **Deirdre** (green, cool strategist) | `Confident_Walk` · 106 | `Gangnam_Groove` · 74 | `Idle_03` · 12 |
| **Decklan** (yellow, showboat) | `Stage_Walk` · 55 | `Shake_It_Off_Dance` · 82 | `Idle_02` · 11 |
| **Gerald** (purple, nervous) | `Unsteady_Walk` · 123 | `FunnyDancing_01` · 22 | `Confused_Scratch` · 36 |

Safe fallbacks if any preset deforms badly on the claws/proportions:
- **Walk:** `Casual_Walk` (30), `Quick_Walk` (115), `Walking_Woman` (1).
- **Dance:** `Cardio_Dance` (70), `You_Groove` (84), `Arm_Circle_Shuffle` (63).
- **Idle:** `Idle` (0), `Idle_02` (11), `Idle_03` (12). Plain `Idle` (0) is the most neutral, loop-clean choice for AR.

Notes:
- All listed presets are in the **biped** library, which matches our Humanoid rig.
- Idle and walk loop cleanly; pick the simplest idle (`Idle` / `Idle_02`) for the default AR Quick Look state, since AR viewers often autoplay the first clip.

---

## 3. Export settings

- **Format:** export **GLB** as the primary deliverable (best for `model-viewer` and for the FBX→USDZ step). FBX only as a fallback / for DCC round-tripping. Meshy outputs both GLB and FBX for every rig and animation.
- **Clips: one per file (Meshy default).** Meshy produces **one animation clip per animation task** — each clip (walk, dance, idle) comes back as its own GLB/FBX, not bundled. So each character yields 3 separate animated GLBs (plus the base rigged GLB). If a single multi-clip GLB is desired for `model-viewer` clip-switching, the clips must be **merged downstream** (e.g. in Blender or with glTF tooling) — Meshy will not emit one GLB with three named clips.
- **USDZ:** Meshy can produce USDZ directly from an animation task via the `fbx2usdz` post-process op (`processed_usdz_url`). This is the fastest path to AR Quick Look and avoids a separate Reality Converter step. Validate the resulting USDZ on-device; if texture/animation issues appear, fall back to converting the animated GLB/FBX in Reality Converter.
- **Frame rate:** default **30 fps**. The API `change_fps` op allows 24/25/30/60. Use **30** (good size/smoothness balance for AR + web); use 60 only if motion looks choppy on a specific dance.
- **Scale:** export at **Meshy default scale** — do not rescale in Meshy. Final 2 cm figure sizing is normalized at conversion time (USDZ placement / model-viewer `scale`/bounds). Just keep the default 1.7 m rig height through export.

Deliverables per character (×5):
- `<name>_rigged.glb` (base rig, no clip)
- `<name>_walk.glb`, `<name>_dance.glb`, `<name>_idle.glb`
- `<name>_idle.usdz` (or walk, whichever is the AR default) via `fbx2usdz`
- FBX equivalents kept as fallback.

---

## 4. API — auto-rigging + animation

Base URL `https://api.meshy.ai`. Auth header `Authorization: Bearer ${MESHY_API_KEY}` on every call. All tasks are async: POST returns a task `id`, then poll `GET .../:id` (or stream `GET .../:id/stream`) until `status` is `SUCCEEDED`. Rig cost ≈ 5 credits per the docs example.

### Endpoints

| Action | Method + path |
|---|---|
| Create rig | `POST /openapi/v1/rigging` |
| Get rig | `GET /openapi/v1/rigging/:id` |
| Stream rig | `GET /openapi/v1/rigging/:id/stream` |
| Delete rig | `DELETE /openapi/v1/rigging/:id` |
| Create animation | `POST /openapi/v1/animations` |
| Get animation | `GET /openapi/v1/animations/:id` |
| Stream animation | `GET /openapi/v1/animations/:id/stream` |
| Animation library (action_id list) | docs: `/en/api/animation-library` |

### Step 1 — rig (one per character)

```bash
curl https://api.meshy.ai/openapi/v1/rigging \
  -X POST \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${MESHY_API_KEY}" \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d '{
    "model_url": "https://YOUR_HOST/clawd.glb",
    "height_meters": 1.7
  }'
```

Response: `{ "result": "<rig_task_id>" }`

Input rules:
- Provide **either** `model_url` (publicly reachable URL or data URI to a textured `.glb`) **or** `input_task_id` (id of a prior Meshy generation task). With `input_task_id`, the ≤300k-face limit is enforced.
- Optional `texture_image_url` (PNG) for the base color, and `height_meters` (default 1.7).
- Face must point +Z; `.glb` only.

Poll until done:

```bash
curl https://api.meshy.ai/openapi/v1/rigging/<rig_task_id> \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${MESHY_API_KEY}"
```

Success `result` contains `rigged_character_glb_url`, `rigged_character_fbx_url`, and a `basic_animations` block with default `walking_*` / `running_*` GLB+FBX URLs. (Asset URLs are pre-signed and **expire** — download promptly.)

### Step 2 — apply each animation clip (3 per character)

```bash
curl https://api.meshy.ai/openapi/v1/animations \
  -X POST \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${MESHY_API_KEY}" \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d '{
    "rig_task_id": "<rig_task_id>",
    "action_id": 0,
    "post_process": { "operation_type": "fbx2usdz" }
  }'
```

- `rig_task_id` — from step 1. `action_id` — the preset integer (e.g. Idle = 0, see section 2 table).
- `post_process.operation_type` ∈ `change_fps` | `fbx2usdz` | `extract_armature`. For `change_fps`, add `"fps": 30` (allowed 24/25/30/60).
- Call this 3× per character (walk id, dance id, idle id). `post_process` is optional; include `fbx2usdz` on whichever clip is the AR default.

Poll `GET /openapi/v1/animations/<id>`. Success `result` contains:
`animation_glb_url`, `animation_fbx_url`, `processed_usdz_url` (if `fbx2usdz`), `processed_armature_fbx_url`, `processed_animation_fps_fbx_url` (if `change_fps`).

### Suggested automation loop (5 chars × 3 clips)

For each character: POST rig → poll to SUCCEEDED → for each of its 3 `action_id`s, POST animation → poll → download GLB (+ USDZ for the AR-default clip). 5 rig tasks + 15 animation tasks total. Mind rate limits (HTTP 429) — serialize or add backoff. Credits are refunded on FAILED tasks.

---

## 5. Known limitations & gotchas

- **Humanoid-only / claws = hands.** Auto-rig only works well on bipedal humanoids with clear limbs. There is no "claws" rig type — Meshy maps claws to the hand/wrist bone. This is acceptable for our walk/dance/idle (no finger articulation needed). Don't expect individual claw-finger bones.
- **300k-face hard limit.** Models over 300k faces are rejected (`400 - Face count exceeded`). Our 320k-tri characters (and any near the ceiling) **must be decimated first** — use Meshy's Remesh API/Blender plugin or decimate in Blender to land comfortably under 300k (target ~150–250k). Triangles ≈ faces here; leave headroom.
- **Pose estimation failure (`422`).** Means Meshy couldn't read it as a humanoid. Fixes: ensure clean A/T-pose, limbs separated from torso, face pointing +Z, upright, symmetrical, single connected textured mesh.
- **Retopology effects.** If you remesh to hit the face limit, re-bake/verify the albedo still maps (UVs may shift). Rig the **decimated, re-textured** mesh, not the original 320k one. Keep the high-res original for any non-AR renders.
- **Non-humanoid proportions.** Big heads, stubby limbs, and claw "hands" can cause minor weight bleed (e.g. claw verts pulled by forearm). Inspect the preview deform; if a limb collapses, try a cleaner A-pose and re-rig, or pick a simpler animation from the fallbacks in section 2.
- **Misplaced skeleton — what to do:** Meshy auto-rig has limited manual joint editing. If bones land wrong: (a) re-export the source in a cleaner T-pose with more limb separation and re-run; (b) adjust `height_meters` if proportions are off; (c) confirm +Z facing and symmetry; (d) as a last resort, rig that character manually in Blender/Mixamo and skip Meshy for that one. Mixamo is a viable fallback for stubborn claw-hand cases (also humanoid auto-rig, similar constraints).
- **Expiring asset URLs.** All result URLs are pre-signed and time-limited — download GLB/FBX/USDZ immediately; don't store the URLs long-term.
- **One clip per task.** No native multi-clip GLB; merge downstream if `model-viewer` clip-switching is required (section 3).
- **AR autoplay.** AR Quick Look / model-viewer typically autoplays the first/only clip. Keep the AR-default USDZ to a clean looping idle or walk.

---

## 6. Handoff checklist for Yash

```
LITTLE SUPERCLAWS — MESHY RIG + ANIMATE (5 chars × walk/dance/idle)

PREP
[ ] Confirm each GLB: single textured mesh, A/T-pose, limbs separated, face pointing +Z, upright & symmetrical.
[ ] Check tri/face count. Any model >300k faces -> decimate to ~150-250k (Meshy Remesh API or Blender), re-verify texture/UVs.
[ ] Host each GLB at a public URL (or use data URI) for the API.

RIG (per character)
[ ] POST /openapi/v1/rigging  { model_url, height_meters: 1.7 }  -> save rig_task_id
[ ] Poll GET /openapi/v1/rigging/:id until SUCCEEDED
[ ] Eyeball preview deform; if 422/misplaced -> fix pose/+Z/symmetry & re-run (Mixamo fallback if stuck)
[ ] Save rigged_character_glb_url

ANIMATE (3 clips per character — action_ids)
[ ] Clawd:   walk 121, dance 79, idle 36
[ ] Nessa:   walk 107, dance 66, idle 255
[ ] Deirdre: walk 106, dance 74, idle 12
[ ] Decklan: walk 55,  dance 82, idle 11
[ ] Gerald:  walk 123, dance 22, idle 36
[ ] POST /openapi/v1/animations { rig_task_id, action_id, post_process:{operation_type:"change_fps", fps:30} }
[ ] For the AR-default clip add post_process {operation_type:"fbx2usdz"} -> grab processed_usdz_url

EXPORT / DELIVER (per character)
[ ] Download GLB for walk/dance/idle (+ base rigged GLB), FBX as fallback
[ ] Download USDZ for AR-default clip
[ ] Keep Meshy default scale (2cm sizing handled at conversion)
[ ] (Optional) merge 3 clips into one multi-clip GLB for model-viewer clip switching

NOTES
- Auth: Authorization: Bearer ${MESHY_API_KEY} on every call. Base: https://api.meshy.ai
- GLB only on input, <=300k faces, .glb. Result URLs expire -> download immediately.
- Tasks are async: POST returns id, poll GET :id (or stream :id/stream) to SUCCEEDED.
- Watch 429 rate limits; credits refunded on FAILED tasks (~5 credits/rig).
- Docs: https://docs.meshy.ai/en/api/rigging  |  /animation  |  /animation-library (full action_id list)
```

---

### Sources
- Auto-Rigging & Animation API: https://docs.meshy.ai/en/api/rigging-and-animation
- Rigging API: https://docs.meshy.ai/en/api/rigging
- Animation API: https://docs.meshy.ai/en/api/animation
- Animation Library Reference (action_id list): https://docs.meshy.ai/en/api/animation-library

import io, sys, numpy as np, trimesh, fast_simplification
def go(glb,out,target=40000):
    m=trimesh.load(glb,process=False)
    g=list(m.geometry.values())[0] if isinstance(m,trimesh.Scene) else m
    V=np.asarray(g.vertices,np.float32); F=np.asarray(g.faces,np.int32)
    UV=np.asarray(g.visual.uv,np.float64); img=g.visual.material.baseColorTexture
    from scipy.spatial import cKDTree
    Vd,Fd=fast_simplification.simplify(V,F,target_count=target)
    _,nn=cKDTree(V).query(Vd,k=1); UVd=UV[nn]
    vis=trimesh.visual.TextureVisuals(uv=UVd, image=img)
    tm=trimesh.Trimesh(vertices=Vd.astype(np.float64),faces=Fd,visual=vis,process=False)
    tm.export(out)
    import os; print(f'{out.split("/")[-1]}: {len(Fd)} tris {os.path.getsize(out)/1e6:.1f}MB')
go(sys.argv[1],sys.argv[2])

# Testing your 5 AR characters tonight

You have five tiny claymation superheroes ready to drop into the real world:

- clawd_40k.usdz
- nessa_40k.usdz
- deirdre_40k.usdz
- decklan_40k.usdz
- gerald_40k.usdz

Each one is about 2cm tall, textured, standing on its feet, and ready for AR. Your iPhone Pro with LiDAR is perfect for this. Below are two paths. Start with Path A tonight. It takes about two minutes and needs zero setup.

---

## Path A — the fast test tonight (recommended, about 2 minutes)

This uses AR Quick Look, which is built into your iPhone. You don't install anything. You just open the file and it appears.

### Step 1 — get a file onto your phone

Easiest way, AirDrop from your Mac:

1. On your Mac, make sure Wi-Fi and Bluetooth are on. Same on your iPhone (and unlock the phone).
2. Find clawd_40k.usdz in Finder.
3. Right-click (or Control-click) the file, choose Share, then AirDrop.
4. Pick your iPhone from the list.
5. On the iPhone, tap Accept. It lands in your Files app (or it may offer to open straight away).

No AirDrop handy? Drop the files into iCloud Drive on the Mac, then open the Files app on your phone and look in iCloud Drive. Same result.

### Step 2 — open it and place your character

1. On the iPhone, open the Files app and tap clawd_40k.usdz.
2. It opens in a preview. Tap the small AR button (top-right, the cube icon) to enter AR mode. It may go straight to AR on its own.
3. Point the camera at a table or floor and move the phone slowly side to side for a second so it can read the surface.
4. When a surface is found, Clawd appears, about 2cm tall, standing on the table.

### Step 3 — adjust him

- Drag with one finger to slide him across the surface.
- Pinch with two fingers to make him bigger or smaller.
- Twist with two fingers to rotate him.
- Double-tap him to snap back to true size (his real 2cm) if you've scaled him by accident.

### Step 4 — record your shot

AR Quick Look doesn't have its own record button, so use the iPhone's built-in screen recorder:

1. Swipe down from the top-right corner to open Control Center.
2. Tap the Screen Recording button (a circle inside a circle). It counts down 3, 2, 1, then records everything on screen.
3. Shoot your scene.
4. To stop, tap the red time pill at the top-left, then Stop. The video saves to Photos.

Tip: turn on Do Not Disturb first so notifications don't pop into your recording.

### Making a tiny figure look believable

- Get low and close. Bring the lens down near table height so you're eye-level with a 2cm hero, not looking down on him.
- Move slowly. Drifting the phone gently sideways gives parallax (near things slide faster than far things), which sells the illusion of real depth.
- Side-light him. Place a lamp low and to one side so he casts a real shadow. Shadow is what glues him to the surface.
- Avoid pure top-down. Straight-down angles flatten everything and kill the sense of scale.
- Use a textured surface. Wood grain or fabric helps tracking lock on and gives a sense of size next to him.

---

## Path B — Reality Composer (for multi-character scenes and repeatable shots)

Use this when you want several characters in one scene, or you want to set up a shot once and come back to the exact same arrangement later.

### The honest state of the app in 2026

Reality Composer for iPhone and iPad is still on the App Store. It's free, made by Apple, and needs iOS 17 or later. It is the right tool for arranging USDZ characters into a scene on your phone.

One thing worth knowing so you don't go looking for the wrong thing: there's a separate tool called Reality Composer Pro. That one is Mac-only and built for app developers preparing content for Apple's Vision Pro headset. You do not need it. For placing your five characters and filming them, the regular Reality Composer app on the iPhone is what you want.

If you ever can't find Reality Composer in the App Store, the best fallback is still Path A above (AR Quick Look), one character at a time. For multiple characters with no special app, you can also place them inside the Clips app, which has an AR mode and records video directly.

### Step 1 — install it

1. Open the App Store on your iPhone.
2. Search for Reality Composer (by Apple).
3. Install it and open it.

### Step 2 — get your files into it

Reality Composer reads USDZ files. Make sure all five are on your phone (AirDrop them like in Path A, or have them in Files/iCloud Drive).

### Step 3 — build a scene

1. Open Reality Composer and start a new project.
2. When it asks for an anchor, choose Horizontal. That tells it your characters live on a flat surface like a table or floor.
3. Add your characters: use the add (+) button, then import from Files, and pick clawd_40k.usdz. Repeat to bring in nessa, deirdre, decklan and gerald.
4. Drag each one where you want it. You can build a little group shot, a face-off, a lineup, whatever you like.
5. Optional and only if it's easy: tap a character, look at Behaviors, and add a simple ready-made one (for example a tap-to-spin or a gentle bounce). Skip this if it's fiddly. It's a bonus, not the point tonight.

### Step 4 — view it in the real world and record

1. Tap AR (or the AR view button) to drop your whole scene onto a real surface through the camera.
2. Move the phone slowly to let it find the surface, same as Path A.
3. Record with the iPhone screen recorder (Control Center, Screen Recording button), exactly as in Path A Step 4.

The same believable-shot tips from Path A apply here: get low, move slowly, side-light, avoid top-down.

---

- [ ] iPhone unlocked, Wi-Fi and Bluetooth on, AirDrop ready.
- [ ] All five USDZ files on the phone (in Files or iCloud Drive).

- File won't open: confirm the name still ends in .usdz, open it from the Files app (not from an email preview), and make sure the phone is on iOS 17 or later.
- Model looks too big or too small: pinch to resize, or double-tap the figure to snap back to true 2cm size.
- No surface detected: point at a well-lit, textured surface (wood, fabric, patterned floor), avoid plain white or shiny tables, and move the phone slowly side to side for a few seconds to let it lock on.

content.content:
1	# Little SuperClaws — Meshy rigging + animation spec
2	
3	Execution-ready spec for rigging and animating the five Little SuperClaws characters in Meshy AI, then exporting rigged GLBs with walk + dance + idle clips for the iPhone AR Quick Look (USDZ) and web `model-viewer` pipeline.
4	
5	Characters: Clawd (blue), Nessa (red), Deirdre (green), Decklan (yellow), Gerald (purple). Source files: single-mesh GLB, one baked albedo texture each, ~160k–320k tris.
6	
7	> Critical fact to know before starting: Meshy auto-rigging only accepts **textured humanoid GLB with ≤300,000 faces**. Several of our models exceed this and need a remesh/decimate pass first. See section 5.
8	
9	---
10	
11	## 1. UI workflow — rigging each character
12	
13	Web app: https://www.meshy.ai → **Animate** (or **Rig & Animate**) workspace.
14	
15	Per character:
16	
17	1. **Pre-checks before upload** (do these to maximize auto-rig success):
18	   - **Single connected mesh, textured.** Meshy will reject untextured meshes and non-humanoid/unclear-limb meshes. Our models are already single-mesh with a baked albedo — good.
19	   - **A/T-pose, limbs separated from torso.** Auto-rig does pose estimation; arms/legs must be clearly distinguishable from the body. Claws spread slightly away from the hips/thighs help; arms angled down-and-out (A-pose) or straight out (T-pose) both work. Avoid limbs fused to the torso or to each other.
20	   - **Facing +Z (glTF forward).** When rigging from a `model_url`/upload, the character's face must point toward +Z. Models facing another axis fail pose estimation. Confirm forward axis in Blender/three before upload.
21	   - **Upright, feet near origin, symmetrical.** Symmetry improves skeleton placement; left/right limbs in mirrored positions.
22	   - **Face count ≤ 300k.** Decimate any model over the limit first (see section 5).
23	2. **Upload** the GLB into the Animate workspace.
24	3. **Set character type / template.** Choose the **Humanoid / Biped** template. There is no separate "claws" template — claws are treated as hands. Pick Humanoid Biped for all five; the wrist/hand bones will land at the claw base (this is fine and is what we want).
25	4. **Set height.** Enter an approximate real-world height to scale the rig. Our figures are tiny but enter a normal humanoid height (e.g. **1.7 m**, the default) — height only affects internal rig scaling/proportion guesses, not final export size. Do **not** enter 0.02 m; that can confuse scaling. Final 2 cm sizing is handled at USDZ/model-viewer conversion.
26	5. **Run auto-rig.** Completes in well under a minute per model. Meshy builds the skeleton and skin weights and previews a default walk on the rigged character.
27	6. **Inspect the skeleton in preview.** Confirm spine, hips, shoulders, elbows, knees, and wrist/claw bones sit roughly correctly and the mesh deforms cleanly on the preview walk. If the skeleton is misplaced, see section 5.
28	7. **Proceed to animation** (section 2) once the rig looks correct.
29	
30	Repeat for all five. Rig each character once; you can then apply many animation clips to that one rig without re-rigging.
31	
32	---
33	
34	## 2. Animation presets per character
35	
36	Meshy exposes a named preset library (500+ clips). Each preset has a stable **`action_id`** integer (used by the API; in the UI you pick the named clip from the **Dancing / Walk & Run / Daily Actions** categories). For every character apply **one walk + one dance + one idle** at minimum. Below are concrete, fitting picks; the agent can swap within the same category to taste.
37	
38	Personality cues: Clawd = anxious leader, Nessa = hot-headed muscle, Deirdre = cool strategist, Decklan = showboat, Gerald = nervous.
39	
40	| Character | Walk (preset · id) | Dance (preset · id) | Idle (preset · id) |
41	|---|---|---|---|
42	| **Clawd** (blue, anxious leader) | `Thoughtful_Walk` · 121 | `OMG_Groove` · 79 | `Confused_Scratch` · 36 |
43	| **Nessa** (red, hot-headed muscle) | `Confident_Strut` · 107 | `Boom_Dance` · 66 | `Angry_Ground_Stomp` · 255 |
44	| **Deirdre** (green, cool strategist) | `Confident_Walk` · 106 | `Gangnam_Groove` · 74 | `Idle_03` · 12 |
45	| **Decklan** (yellow, showboat) | `Stage_Walk` · 55 | `Shake_It_Off_Dance` · 82 | `Idle_02` · 11 |
46	| **Gerald** (purple, nervous) | `Unsteady_Walk` · 123 | `FunnyDancing_01` · 22 | `Confused_Scratch` · 36 |
47	
48	Safe fallbacks if any preset deforms badly on the claws/proportions:
49	- **Walk:** `Casual_Walk` (30), `Quick_Walk` (115), `Walking_Woman` (1).
50	- **Dance:** `Cardio_Dance` (70), `You_Groove` (84), `Arm_Circle_Shuffle` (63).
51	- **Idle:** `Idle` (0), `Idle_02` (11), `Idle_03` (12). Plain `Idle` (0) is the most neutral, loop-clean choice for AR.
52	
53	Notes:
54	- All listed presets are in the **biped** library, which matches our Humanoid rig.
55	- Idle and walk loop cleanly; pick the simplest idle (`Idle` / `Idle_02`) for the default AR Quick Look state, since AR viewers often autoplay the first clip.
56	
57	---
58	
59	## 3. Export settings
60	
61	- **Format:** export **GLB** as the primary deliverable (best for `model-viewer` and for the FBX→USDZ step). FBX only as a fallback / for DCC round-tripping. Meshy outputs both GLB and FBX for every rig and animation.
62	- **Clips: one per file (Meshy default).** Meshy produces **one animation clip per animation task** — each clip (walk, dance, idle) comes back as its own GLB/FBX, not bundled. So each character yields 3 separate animated GLBs (plus the base rigged GLB). If a single multi-clip GLB is desired for `model-viewer` clip-switching, the clips must be **merged downstream** (e.g. in Blender or with glTF tooling) — Meshy will not emit one GLB with three named clips.
63	- **USDZ:** Meshy can produce USDZ directly from an animation task via the `fbx2usdz` post-process op (`processed_usdz_url`). This is the fastest path to AR Quick Look and avoids a separate Reality Converter step. Validate the resulting USDZ on-device; if texture/animation issues appear, fall back to converting the animated GLB/FBX in Reality Converter.
64	- **Frame rate:** default **30 fps**. The API `change_fps` op allows 24/25/30/60. Use **30** (good size/smoothness balance for AR + web); use 60 only if motion looks choppy on a specific dance.
65	- **Scale:** export at **Meshy default scale** — do not rescale in Meshy. Final 2 cm figure sizing is normalized at conversion time (USDZ placement / model-viewer `scale`/bounds). Just keep the default 1.7 m rig height through export.
66	
67	Deliverables per character (×5):
68	- `<name>_rigged.glb` (base rig, no clip)
69	- `<name>_walk.glb`, `<name>_dance.glb`, `<name>_idle.glb`
70	- `<name>_idle.usdz` (or walk, whichever is the AR default) via `fbx2usdz`
71	- FBX equivalents kept as fallback.
72	
73	---
74	
75	## 4. API — auto-rigging + animation
76	
77	Base URL `https://api.meshy.ai`. Auth header `Authorization: Bearer ${MESHY_API_KEY}` on every call. All tasks are async: POST returns a task `id`, then poll `GET .../:id` (or stream `GET .../:id/stream`) until `status` is `SUCCEEDED`. Rig cost ≈ 5 credits per the docs example.
78	
79	### Endpoints
80	
81	| Action | Method + path |
82	|---|---|
83	| Create rig | `POST /openapi/v1/rigging` |
84	| Get rig | `GET /openapi/v1/rigging/:id` |
85	| Stream rig | `GET /openapi/v1/rigging/:id/stream` |
86	| Delete rig | `DELETE /openapi/v1/rigging/:id` |
87	| Create animation | `POST /openapi/v1/animations` |
88	| Get animation | `GET /openapi/v1/animations/:id` |
89	| Stream animation | `GET /openapi/v1/animations/:id/stream` |
90	| Animation library (action_id list) | docs: `/en/api/animation-library` |
91	
92	### Step 1 — rig (one per character)
93	
94	```bash
95	curl https://api.meshy.ai/openapi/v1/rigging \
96	  -X POST \
97	  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${MESHY_API_KEY}" \
98	  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
99	  -d '{
100	    "model_url": "https://YOUR_HOST/clawd.glb",
101	    "height_meters": 1.7
102	  }'
103	```
104	
105	Response: `{ "result": "<rig_task_id>" }`
106	
107	Input rules:
108	- Provide **either** `model_url` (publicly reachable URL or data URI to a textured `.glb`) **or** `input_task_id` (id of a prior Meshy generation task). With `input_task_id`, the ≤300k-face limit is enforced.
109	- Optional `texture_image_url` (PNG) for the base color, and `height_meters` (default 1.7).
110	- Face must point +Z; `.glb` only.
111	
112	Poll until done:
113	
114	```bash
115	curl https://api.meshy.ai/openapi/v1/rigging/<rig_task_id> \
116	  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${MESHY_API_KEY}"
117	```
118	
119	Success `result` contains `rigged_character_glb_url`, `rigged_character_fbx_url`, and a `basic_animations` block with default `walking_*` / `running_*` GLB+FBX URLs. (Asset URLs are pre-signed and **expire** — download promptly.)
120	
121	### Step 2 — apply each animation clip (3 per character)
122	
123	```bash
124	curl https://api.meshy.ai/openapi/v1/animations \
125	  -X POST \
126	  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${MESHY_API_KEY}" \
127	  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
128	  -d '{
129	    "rig_task_id": "<rig_task_id>",
130	    "action_id": 0,
131	    "post_process": { "operation_type": "fbx2usdz" }
132	  }'
133	```
134	
135	- `rig_task_id` — from step 1. `action_id` — the preset integer (e.g. Idle = 0, see section 2 table).
136	- `post_process.operation_type` ∈ `change_fps` | `fbx2usdz` | `extract_armature`. For `change_fps`, add `"fps": 30` (allowed 24/25/30/60).
137	- Call this 3× per character (walk id, dance id, idle id). `post_process` is optional; include `fbx2usdz` on whichever clip is the AR default.
138	
139	Poll `GET /openapi/v1/animations/<id>`. Success `result` contains:
140	`animation_glb_url`, `animation_fbx_url`, `processed_usdz_url` (if `fbx2usdz`), `processed_armature_fbx_url`, `processed_animation_fps_fbx_url` (if `change_fps`).
141	
142	### Suggested automation loop (5 chars × 3 clips)
143	
144	For each character: POST rig → poll to SUCCEEDED → for each of its 3 `action_id`s, POST animation → poll → download GLB (+ USDZ for the AR-default clip). 5 rig tasks + 15 animation tasks total. Mind rate limits (HTTP 429) — serialize or add backoff. Credits are refunded on FAILED tasks.
145	
146	---
147	
148	## 5. Known limitations & gotchas
149	
150	- **Humanoid-only / claws = hands.** Auto-rig only works well on bipedal humanoids with clear limbs. There is no "claws" rig type — Meshy maps claws to the hand/wrist bone. This is acceptable for our walk/dance/idle (no finger articulation needed). Don't expect individual claw-finger bones.
151	- **300k-face hard limit.** Models over 300k faces are rejected (`400 - Face count exceeded`). Our 320k-tri characters (and any near the ceiling) **must be decimated first** — use Meshy's Remesh API/Blender plugin or decimate in Blender to land comfortably under 300k (target ~150–250k). Triangles ≈ faces here; leave headroom.
152	- **Pose estimation failure (`422`).** Means Meshy couldn't read it as a humanoid. Fixes: ensure clean A/T-pose, limbs separated from torso, face pointing +Z, upright, symmetrical, single connected textured mesh.
153	- **Retopology effects.** If you remesh to hit the face limit, re-bake/verify the albedo still maps (UVs may shift). Rig the **decimated, re-textured** mesh, not the original 320k one. Keep the high-res original for any non-AR renders.
154	- **Non-humanoid proportions.** Big heads, stubby limbs, and claw "hands" can cause minor weight bleed (e.g. claw verts pulled by forearm). Inspect the preview deform; if a limb collapses, try a cleaner A-pose and re-rig, or pick a simpler animation from the fallbacks in section 2.
155	- **Misplaced skeleton — what to do:** Meshy auto-rig has limited manual joint editing. If bones land wrong: (a) re-export the source in a cleaner T-pose with more limb separation and re-run; (b) adjust `height_meters` if proportions are off; (c) confirm +Z facing and symmetry; (d) as a last resort, rig that character manually in Blender/Mixamo and skip Meshy for that one. Mixamo is a viable fallback for stubborn claw-hand cases (also humanoid auto-rig, similar constraints).
156	- **Expiring asset URLs.** All result URLs are pre-signed and time-limited — download GLB/FBX/USDZ immediately; don't store the URLs long-term.
157	- **One clip per task.** No native multi-clip GLB; merge downstream if `model-viewer` clip-switching is required (section 3).
158	- **AR autoplay.** AR Quick Look / model-viewer typically autoplays the first/only clip. Keep the AR-default USDZ to a clean looping idle or walk.
159

1	# Little SuperClaws — Meshy rigging + animation spec
2	
3	Execution-ready spec for rigging and animating the five Little SuperClaws characters in Meshy AI, then exporting rigged GLBs with walk + dance + idle clips for the iPhone AR Quick Look (USDZ) and web `model-viewer` pipeline.
4	
5	Characters: Clawd (blue), Nessa (red), Deirdre (green), Decklan (yellow), Gerald (purple). Source files: single-mesh GLB, one baked albedo texture each, ~160k–320k tris.
6	
7	> Critical fact to know before starting: Meshy auto-rigging only accepts **textured humanoid GLB with ≤300,000 faces**. Several of our models exceed this and need a remesh/decimate pass first. See section 5.
8	
9	---
10	
11	## 1. UI workflow — rigging each character
12	
13	Web app: https://www.meshy.ai → **Animate** (or **Rig & Animate**) workspace.
14	
15	Per character:
16	
17	1. **Pre-checks before upload** (do these to maximize auto-rig success):
18	   - **Single connected mesh, textured.** Meshy will reject untextured meshes and non-humanoid/unclear-limb meshes. Our models are already single-mesh with a baked albedo — good.
19	   - **A/T-pose, limbs separated from torso.** Auto-rig does pose estimation; arms/legs must be clearly distinguishable from the body. Claws spread slightly away from the hips/thighs help; arms angled down-and-out (A-pose) or straight out (T-pose) both work. Avoid limbs fused to the torso or to each other.
20	   - **Facing +Z (glTF forward).** When rigging from a `model_url`/upload, the character's face must point toward +Z. Models facing another axis fail pose estimation. Confirm forward axis in Blender/three before upload.
21	   - **Upright, feet near origin, symmetrical.** Symmetry improves skeleton placement; left/right limbs in mirrored positions.
22	   - **Face count ≤ 300k.** Decimate any model over the limit first (see section 5).
23	2. **Upload** the GLB into the Animate workspace.
24	3. **Set character type / template.** Choose the **Humanoid / Biped** template. There is no separate "claws" template — claws are treated as hands. Pick Humanoid Biped for all five; the wrist/hand bones will land at the claw base (this is fine and is what we want).
25	4. **Set height.** Enter an approximate real-world height to scale the rig. Our figures are tiny but enter a normal humanoid height (e.g. **1.7 m**, the default) — height only affects internal rig scaling/proportion guesses, not final export size. Do **not** enter 0.02 m; that can confuse scaling. Final 2 cm sizing is handled at USDZ/model-viewer conversion.
26	5. **Run auto-rig.** Completes in well under a minute per model. Meshy builds the skeleton and skin weights and previews a default walk on the rigged character.
27	6. **Inspect the skeleton in preview.** Confirm spine, hips, shoulders, elbows, knees, and wrist/claw bones sit roughly correctly and the mesh deforms cleanly on the preview walk. If the skeleton is misplaced, see section 5.
28	7. **Proceed to animation** (section 2) once the rig looks correct.
29	
30	Repeat for all five. Rig each character once; you can then apply many animation clips to that one rig without re-rigging.
31	
32	---
33	
34	## 2. Animation presets per character
35	
36	Meshy exposes a named preset library (500+ clips). Each preset has a stable **`action_id`** integer (used by the API; in the UI you pick the named clip from the **Dancing / Walk & Run / Daily Actions** categories). For every character apply **one walk + one dance + one idle** at minimum. Below are concrete, fitting picks; the agent can swap within the same category to taste.
37	
38	Personality cues: Clawd = anxious leader, Nessa = hot-headed muscle, Deirdre = cool strategist, Decklan = showboat, Gerald = nervous.
39	
40	| Character | Walk (preset · id) | Dance (preset · id) | Idle (preset · id) |
41	|---|---|---|---|
42	| **Clawd** (blue, anxious leader) | `Thoughtful_Walk` · 121 | `OMG_Groove` · 79 | `Confused_Scratch` · 36 |
43	| **Nessa** (red, hot-headed muscle) | `Confident_Strut` · 107 | `Boom_Dance` · 66 | `Angry_Ground_Stomp` · 255 |
44	| **Deirdre** (green, cool strategist) | `Confident_Walk` · 106 | `Gangnam_Groove` · 74 | `Idle_03` · 12 |
45	| **Decklan** (yellow, showboat) | `Stage_Walk` · 55 | `Shake_It_Off_Dance` · 82 | `Idle_02` · 11 |
46	| **Gerald** (purple, nervous) | `Unsteady_Walk` · 123 | `FunnyDancing_01` · 22 | `Confused_Scratch` · 36 |
47	
48	Safe fallbacks if any preset deforms badly on the claws/proportions:
49	- **Walk:** `Casual_Walk` (30), `Quick_Walk` (115), `Walking_Woman` (1).
50	- **Dance:** `Cardio_Dance` (70), `You_Groove` (84), `Arm_Circle_Shuffle` (63).
51	- **Idle:** `Idle` (0), `Idle_02` (11), `Idle_03` (12). Plain `Idle` (0) is the most neutral, loop-clean choice for AR.
52	
53	Notes:
54	- All listed presets are in the **biped** library, which matches our Humanoid rig.
55	- Idle and walk loop cleanly; pick the simplest idle (`Idle` / `Idle_02`) for the default AR Quick Look state, since AR viewers often autoplay the first clip.
56	
57	---
58	
59	## 3. Export settings
60	
61	- **Format:** export **GLB** as the primary deliverable (best for `model-viewer` and for the FBX→USDZ step). FBX only as a fallback / for DCC round-tripping. Meshy outputs both GLB and FBX for every rig and animation.
62	- **Clips: one per file (Meshy default).** Meshy produces **one animation clip per animation task** — each clip (walk, dance, idle) comes back as its own GLB/FBX, not bundled. So each character yields 3 separate animated GLBs (plus the base rigged GLB). If a single multi-clip GLB is desired for `model-viewer` clip-switching, the clips must be **merged downstream** (e.g. in Blender or with glTF tooling) — Meshy will not emit one GLB with three named clips.
63	- **USDZ:** Meshy can produce USDZ directly from an animation task via the `fbx2usdz` post-process op (`processed_usdz_url`). This is the fastest path to AR Quick Look and avoids a separate Reality Converter step. Validate the resulting USDZ on-device; if texture/animation issues appear, fall back to converting the animated GLB/FBX in Reality Converter.
64	- **Frame rate:** default **30 fps**. The API `change_fps` op allows 24/25/30/60. Use **30** (good size/smoothness balance for AR + web); use 60 only if motion looks choppy on a specific dance.
65	- **Scale:** export at **Meshy default scale** — do not rescale in Meshy. Final 2 cm figure sizing is normalized at conversion time (USDZ placement / model-viewer `scale`/bounds). Just keep the default 1.7 m rig height through export.
66	
67	Deliverables per character (×5):
68	- `<name>_rigged.glb` (base rig, no clip)
69	- `<name>_walk.glb`, `<name>_dance.glb`, `<name>_idle.glb`
70	- `<name>_idle.usdz` (or walk, whichever is the AR default) via `fbx2usdz`
71	- FBX equivalents kept as fallback.
72	
73	---
74	
75	## 4. API — auto-rigging + animation
76	
77	Base URL `https://api.meshy.ai`. Auth header `Authorization: Bearer ${MESHY_API_KEY}` on every call. All tasks are async: POST returns a task `id`, then poll `GET .../:id` (or stream `GET .../:id/stream`) until `status` is `SUCCEEDED`. Rig cost ≈ 5 credits per the docs example.
78	
79	### Endpoints
80	
81	| Action | Method + path |
82	|---|---|
83	| Create rig | `POST /openapi/v1/rigging` |
84	| Get rig | `GET /openapi/v1/rigging/:id` |
85	| Stream rig | `GET /openapi/v1/rigging/:id/stream` |
86	| Delete rig | `DELETE /openapi/v1/rigging/:id` |
87	| Create animation | `POST /openapi/v1/animations` |
88	| Get animation | `GET /openapi/v1/animations/:id` |
89	| Stream animation | `GET /openapi/v1/animations/:id/stream` |
90	| Animation library (action_id list) | docs: `/en/api/animation-library` |
91	
92	### Step 1 — rig (one per character)
93	
94	```bash
95	curl https://api.meshy.ai/openapi/v1/rigging \
96	  -X POST \
97	  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${MESHY_API_KEY}" \
98	  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
99	  -d '{
100	    "model_url": "https://YOUR_HOST/clawd.glb",
101	    "height_meters": 1.7
102	  }'
103	```
104	
105	Response: `{ "result": "<rig_task_id>" }`
106	
107	Input rules:
108	- Provide **either** `model_url` (publicly reachable URL or data URI to a textured `.glb`) **or** `input_task_id` (id of a prior Meshy generation task). With `input_task_id`, the ≤300k-face limit is enforced.
109	- Optional `texture_image_url` (PNG) for the base color, and `height_meters` (default 1.7).
110	- Face must point +Z; `.glb` only.
111	
112	Poll until done:
113	
114	```bash
115	curl https://api.meshy.ai/openapi/v1/rigging/<rig_task_id> \
116	  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${MESHY_API_KEY}"
117	```
118	
119	Success `result` contains `rigged_character_glb_url`, `rigged_character_fbx_url`, and a `basic_animations` block with default `walking_*` / `running_*` GLB+FBX URLs. (Asset URLs are pre-signed and **expire** — download promptly.)
120	
121	### Step 2 — apply each animation clip (3 per character)
122	
123	```bash
124	curl https://api.meshy.ai/openapi/v1/animations \
125	  -X POST \
126	  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${MESHY_API_KEY}" \
127	  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
128	  -d '{
129	    "rig_task_id": "<rig_task_id>",
130	    "action_id": 0,
131	    "post_process": { "operation_type": "fbx2usdz" }
132	  }'
133	```
134	
135	- `rig_task_id` — from step 1. `action_id` — the preset integer (e.g. Idle = 0, see section 2 table).
136	- `post_process.operation_type` ∈ `change_fps` | `fbx2usdz` | `extract_armature`. For `change_fps`, add `"fps": 30` (allowed 24/25/30/60).
137	- Call this 3× per character (walk id, dance id, idle id). `post_process` is optional; include `fbx2usdz` on whichever clip is the AR default.
138	
139	Poll `GET /openapi/v1/animations/<id>`. Success `result` contains:
140	`animation_glb_url`, `animation_fbx_url`, `processed_usdz_url` (if `fbx2usdz`), `processed_armature_fbx_url`, `processed_animation_fps_fbx_url` (if `change_fps`).
141	
142	### Suggested automation loop (5 chars × 3 clips)
143	
144	For each character: POST rig → poll to SUCCEEDED → for each of its 3 `action_id`s, POST animation → poll → download GLB (+ USDZ for the AR-default clip). 5 rig tasks + 15 animation tasks total. Mind rate limits (HTTP 429) — serialize or add backoff. Credits are refunded on FAILED tasks.
145	
146	---
147	
148	## 5. Known limitations & gotchas
149	
150	- **Humanoid-only / claws = hands.** Auto-rig only works well on bipedal humanoids with clear limbs. There is no "claws" rig type — Meshy maps claws to the hand/wrist bone. This is acceptable for our walk/dance/idle (no finger articulation needed). Don't expect individual claw-finger bones.
151	- **300k-face hard limit.** Models over 300k faces are rejected (`400 - Face count exceeded`). Our 320k-tri characters (and any near the ceiling) **must be decimated first** — use Meshy's Remesh API/Blender plugin or decimate in Blender to land comfortably under 300k (target ~150–250k). Triangles ≈ faces here; leave headroom.
152	- **Pose estimation failure (`422`).** Means Meshy couldn't read it as a humanoid. Fixes: ensure clean A/T-pose, limbs separated from torso, face pointing +Z, upright, symmetrical, single connected textured mesh.
153	- **Retopology effects.** If you remesh to hit the face limit, re-bake/verify the albedo still maps (UVs may shift). Rig the **decimated, re-textured** mesh, not the original 320k one. Keep the high-res original for any non-AR renders.
154	- **Non-humanoid proportions.** Big heads, stubby limbs, and claw "hands" can cause minor weight bleed (e.g. claw verts pulled by forearm). Inspect the preview deform; if a limb collapses, try a cleaner A-pose and re-rig, or pick a simpler animation from the fallbacks in section 2.
155	- **Misplaced skeleton — what to do:** Meshy auto-rig has limited manual joint editing. If bones land wrong: (a) re-export the source in a cleaner T-pose with more limb separation and re-run; (b) adjust `height_meters` if proportions are off; (c) confirm +Z facing and symmetry; (d) as a last resort, rig that character manually in Blender/Mixamo and skip Meshy for that one. Mixamo is a viable fallback for stubborn claw-hand cases (also humanoid auto-rig, similar constraints).
156	- **Expiring asset URLs.** All result URLs are pre-signed and time-limited — download GLB/FBX/USDZ immediately; don't store the URLs long-term.
157	- **One clip per task.** No native multi-clip GLB; merge downstream if `model-viewer` clip-switching is required (section 3).
158	- **AR autoplay.** AR Quick Look / model-viewer typically autoplays the first/only clip. Keep the AR-default USDZ to a clean looping idle or walk.
159	
160	---
161	
162	## 6. Handoff checklist for Yash
163	
164	```
165	LITTLE SUPERCLAWS — MESHY RIG + ANIMATE (5 chars × walk/dance/idle)
166	
167	PREP
168	[ ] Confirm each GLB: single textured mesh, A/T-pose, limbs separated, face pointing +Z, upright & symmetrical.
169	[ ] Check tri/face count. Any model >300k faces -> decimate to ~150-250k (Meshy Remesh API or Blender), re-verify texture/UVs.
170	[ ] Host each GLB at a public URL (or use data URI) for the API.
171	
172	RIG (per character)
173	[ ] POST /openapi/v1/rigging  { model_url, height_meters: 1.7 }  -> save rig_task_id
174	[ ] Poll GET /openapi/v1/rigging/:id until SUCCEEDED
175	[ ] Eyeball preview deform; if 422/misplaced -> fix pose/+Z/symmetry & re-run (Mixamo fallback if stuck)
176	[ ] Save rigged_character_glb_url
177	
178	ANIMATE (3 clips per character — action_ids)
179	[ ] Clawd:   walk 121, dance 79, idle 36
180	[ ] Nessa:   walk 107, dance 66, idle 255
181	[ ] Deirdre: walk 106, dance 74, idle 12
182	[ ] Decklan: walk 55,  dance 82, idle 11
183	[ ] Gerald:  walk 123, dance 22, idle 36
184	[ ] POST /openapi/v1/animations { rig_task_id, action_id, post_process:{operation_type:"change_fps", fps:30} }
185	[ ] For the AR-default clip add post_process {operation_type:"fbx2usdz"} -> grab processed_usdz_url
186	
187	EXPORT / DELIVER (per character)
188	[ ] Download GLB for walk/dance/idle (+ base rigged GLB), FBX as fallback
189	[ ] Download USDZ for AR-default clip
190	[ ] Keep Meshy default scale (2cm sizing handled at conversion)
191	[ ] (Optional) merge 3 clips into one multi-clip GLB for model-viewer clip switching
192	
193	NOTES
194	- Auth: Authorization: Bearer ${MESHY_API_KEY} on every call. Base: https://api.meshy.ai
195	- GLB only on input, <=300k faces, .glb. Result URLs expire -> download immediately.
196	- Tasks are async: POST returns id, poll GET :id (or stream :id/stream) to SUCCEEDED.
197	- Watch 429 rate limits; credits refunded on FAILED tasks (~5 credits/rig).
198	- Docs: https://docs.meshy.ai/en/api/rigging  |  /animation  |  /animation-library (full action_id list)
199	```

> Critical fact to know before starting: Meshy auto-rigging only accepts **textured humanoid GLB with ≤300,000 faces**. Several of our models exceed this and need a remesh/decimate pass first. See section 5.

---

## 1. UI workflow — rigging each character

Web app: https://www.meshy.ai → **Animate** (or **Rig & Animate**) workspace.

Per character:

1. **Pre-checks before upload** (do these to maximize auto-rig success):
   - **Single connected mesh, textured.** Meshy will reject untextured meshes and non-humanoid/unclear-limb meshes. Our models are already single-mesh with a baked albedo — good.
   - **A/T-pose, limbs separated from torso.** Auto-rig does pose estimation; arms/legs must be clearly distinguishable from the body. Claws spread slightly away from the hips/thighs help; arms angled down-and-out (A-pose) or straight out (T-pose) both work. Avoid limbs fused to the torso or to each other.
   - **Facing +Z (glTF forward).** When rigging from a `model_url`/upload, the character's face must point toward +Z. Models facing another axis fail pose estimation. Confirm forward axis in Blender/three before upload.
   - **Upright, feet near origin, symmetrical.** Symmetry improves skeleton placement; left/right limbs in mirrored positions.
   - **Face count ≤ 300k.** Decimate any model over the limit first (see section 5).
2. **Upload** the GLB into the Animate workspace.
3. **Set character type / template.** Choose the **Humanoid / Biped** template. There is no separate "claws" template — claws are treated as hands. Pick Humanoid Biped for all five; the wrist/hand bones will land at the claw base (this is fine and is what we want).
4. **Set height.** Enter an approximate real-world height to scale the rig. Our figures are tiny but enter a normal humanoid height (e.g. **1.7 m**, the default) — height only affects internal rig scaling/proportion guesses, not final export size. Do **not** enter 0.02 m; that can confuse scaling. Final 2 cm sizing is handled at USDZ/model-viewer conversion.
5. **Run auto-rig.** Completes in well under a minute per model. Meshy builds the skeleton and skin weights and previews a default walk on the rigged character.
6. **Inspect the skeleton in preview.** Confirm spine, hips, shoulders, elbows, knees, and wrist/claw bones sit roughly correctly and the mesh deforms cleanly on the preview walk. If the skeleton is misplaced, see section 5.
7. **Proceed to animation** (section 2) once the rig looks correct.

Repeat for all five. Rig each character once; you can then apply many animation clips to that one rig without re-rigging.

---

## 2. Animation presets per character

Meshy exposes a named preset library (500+ clips). Each preset has a stable **`action_id`** integer (used by the API; in the UI you pick the named clip from the **Dancing / Walk & Run / Daily Actions** categories). For every character apply **one walk + one dance + one idle** at minimum. Below are concrete, fitting picks; the agent can swap within the same category to taste.

Personality cues: Clawd = anxious leader, Nessa = hot-headed muscle, Deirdre = cool strategist, Decklan = showboat, Gerald = nervous.

| Character | Walk (preset · id) | Dance (preset · id) | Idle (preset · id) |
|---|---|---|---|
| **Clawd** (blue, anxious leader) | `Thoughtful_Walk` · 121 | `OMG_Groove` · 79 | `Confused_Scratch` · 36 |
| **Nessa** (red, hot-headed muscle) | `Confident_Strut` · 107 | `Boom_Dance` · 66 | `Angry_Ground_Stomp` · 255 |
| **Deirdre** (green, cool strategist) | `Confident_Walk` · 106 | `Gangnam_Groove` · 74 | `Idle_03` · 12 |
| **Decklan** (yellow, showboat) | `Stage_Walk` · 55 | `Shake_It_Off_Dance` · 82 | `Idle_02` · 11 |
| **Gerald** (purple, nervous) | `Unsteady_Walk` · 123 | `FunnyDancing_01` · 22 | `Confused_Scratch` · 36 |

Safe fallbacks if any preset deforms badly on the claws/proportions:
- **Walk:** `Casual_Walk` (30), `Quick_Walk` (115), `Walking_Woman` (1).
- **Dance:** `Cardio_Dance` (70), `You_Groove` (84), `Arm_Circle_Shuffle` (63).
- **Idle:** `Idle` (0), `Idle_02` (11), `Idle_03` (12). Plain `Idle` (0) is the most neutral, loop-clean choice for AR.

Notes:
- All listed presets are in the **biped** library, which matches our Humanoid rig.
- Idle and walk loop cleanly; pick the simplest idle (`Idle` / `Idle_02`) for the default AR Quick Look state, since AR viewers often autoplay the first clip.

---

## 3. Export settings

- **Format:** export **GLB** as the primary deliverable (best for `model-viewer` and for the FBX→USDZ step). FBX only as a fallback / for DCC round-tripping. Meshy outputs both GLB and FBX for every rig and animation.
- **Clips: one per file (Meshy default).** Meshy produces **one animation clip per animation task** — each clip (walk, dance, idle) comes back as its own GLB/FBX, not bundled. So each character yields 3 separate animated GLBs (plus the base rigged GLB). If a single multi-clip GLB is desired for `model-viewer` clip-switching, the clips must be **merged downstream** (e.g. in Blender or with glTF tooling) — Meshy will not emit one GLB with three named clips.
- **USDZ:** Meshy can produce USDZ directly from an animation task via the `fbx2usdz` post-process op (`processed_usdz_url`). This is the fastest path to AR Quick Look and avoids a separate Reality Converter step. Validate the resulting USDZ on-device; if texture/animation issues appear, fall back to converting the animated GLB/FBX in Reality Converter.
- **Frame rate:** default **30 fps**. The API `change_fps` op allows 24/25/30/60. Use **30** (good size/smoothness balance for AR + web); use 60 only if motion looks choppy on a specific dance.
- **Scale:** export at **Meshy default scale** — do not rescale in Meshy. Final 2 cm figure sizing is normalized at conversion time (USDZ placement / model-viewer `scale`/bounds). Just keep the default 1.7 m rig height through export.

Deliverables per character (×5):
- `<name>_rigged.glb` (base rig, no clip)
- `<name>_walk.glb`, `<name>_dance.glb`, `<name>_idle.glb`
- `<name>_idle.usdz` (or walk, whichever is the AR default) via `fbx2usdz`
- FBX equivalents kept as fallback.

---

## 4. API — auto-rigging + animation

Base URL `https://api.meshy.ai`. Auth header `Authorization: Bearer ${MESHY_API_KEY}` on every call. All tasks are async: POST returns a task `id`, then poll `GET .../:id` (or stream `GET .../:id/stream`) until `status` is `SUCCEEDED`. Rig cost ≈ 5 credits per the docs example.

### Endpoints

| Action | Method + path |
|---|---|
| Create rig | `POST /openapi/v1/rigging` |
| Get rig | `GET /openapi/v1/rigging/:id` |
| Stream rig | `GET /openapi/v1/rigging/:id/stream` |
| Delete rig | `DELETE /openapi/v1/rigging/:id` |
| Create animation | `POST /openapi/v1/animations` |
| Get animation | `GET /openapi/v1/animations/:id` |
| Stream animation | `GET /openapi/v1/animations/:id/stream` |
| Animation library (action_id list) | docs: `/en/api/animation-library` |

### Step 1 — rig (one per character)

```bash
curl https://api.meshy.ai/openapi/v1/rigging \
  -X POST \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${MESHY_API_KEY}" \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d '{
    "model_url": "https://YOUR_HOST/clawd.glb",
    "height_meters": 1.7
  }'
```

Response: `{ "result": "<rig_task_id>" }`

Input rules:
- Provide **either** `model_url` (publicly reachable URL or data URI to a textured `.glb`) **or** `input_task_id` (id of a prior Meshy generation task). With `input_task_id`, the ≤300k-face limit is enforced.
- Optional `texture_image_url` (PNG) for the base color, and `height_meters` (default 1.7).
- Face must point +Z; `.glb` only.

Poll until done:

```bash
curl https://api.meshy.ai/openapi/v1/rigging/<rig_task_id> \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${MESHY_API_KEY}"
```

Success `result` contains `rigged_character_glb_url`, `rigged_character_fbx_url`, and a `basic_animations` block with default `walking_*` / `running_*` GLB+FBX URLs. (Asset URLs are pre-signed and **expire** — download promptly.)

### Step 2 — apply each animation clip (3 per character)

```bash
curl https://api.meshy.ai/openapi/v1/animations \
  -X POST \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${MESHY_API_KEY}" \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d '{
    "rig_task_id": "<rig_task_id>",
    "action_id": 0,
    "post_process": { "operation_type": "fbx2usdz" }
  }'
```

- `rig_task_id` — from step 1. `action_id` — the preset integer (e.g. Idle = 0, see section 2 table).
- `post_process.operation_type` ∈ `change_fps` | `fbx2usdz` | `extract_armature`. For `change_fps`, add `"fps": 30` (allowed 24/25/30/60).
- Call this 3× per character (walk id, dance id, idle id). `post_process` is optional; include `fbx2usdz` on whichever clip is the AR default.

Poll `GET /openapi/v1/animations/<id>`. Success `result` contains:
`animation_glb_url`, `animation_fbx_url`, `processed_usdz_url` (if `fbx2usdz`), `processed_armature_fbx_url`, `processed_animation_fps_fbx_url` (if `change_fps`).

### Suggested automation loop (5 chars × 3 clips)

For each character: POST rig → poll to SUCCEEDED → for each of its 3 `action_id`s, POST animation → poll → download GLB (+ USDZ for the AR-default clip). 5 rig tasks + 15 animation tasks total. Mind rate limits (HTTP 429) — serialize or add backoff. Credits are refunded on FAILED tasks.

---

## 5. Known limitations & gotchas

- **Humanoid-only / claws = hands.** Auto-rig only works well on bipedal humanoids with clear limbs. There is no "claws" rig type — Meshy maps claws to the hand/wrist bone. This is acceptable for our walk/dance/idle (no finger articulation needed). Don't expect individual claw-finger bones.
- **300k-face hard limit.** Models over 300k faces are rejected (`400 - Face count exceeded`). Our 320k-tri characters (and any near the ceiling) **must be decimated first** — use Meshy's Remesh API/Blender plugin or decimate in Blender to land comfortably under 300k (target ~150–250k). Triangles ≈ faces here; leave headroom.
- **Pose estimation failure (`422`).** Means Meshy couldn't read it as a humanoid. Fixes: ensure clean A/T-pose, limbs separated from torso, face pointing +Z, upright, symmetrical, single connected textured mesh.
- **Retopology effects.** If you remesh to hit the face limit, re-bake/verify the albedo still maps (UVs may shift). Rig the **decimated, re-textured** mesh, not the original 320k one. Keep the high-res original for any non-AR renders.
- **Non-humanoid proportions.** Big heads, stubby limbs, and claw "hands" can cause minor weight bleed (e.g. claw verts pulled by forearm). Inspect the preview deform; if a limb collapses, try a cleaner A-pose and re-rig, or pick a simpler animation from the fallbacks in section 2.
- **Misplaced skeleton — what to do:** Meshy auto-rig has limited manual joint editing. If bones land wrong: (a) re-export the source in a cleaner T-pose with more limb separation and re-run; (b) adjust `height_meters` if proportions are off; (c) confirm +Z facing and symmetry; (d) as a last resort, rig that character manually in Blender/Mixamo and skip Meshy for that one. Mixamo is a viable fallback for stubborn claw-hand cases (also humanoid auto-rig, similar constraints).
- **Expiring asset URLs.** All result URLs are pre-signed and time-limited — download GLB/FBX/USDZ immediately; don't store the URLs long-term.
- **One clip per task.** No native multi-clip GLB; merge downstream if `model-viewer` clip-switching is required (section 3).
- **AR autoplay.** AR Quick Look / model-viewer typically autoplays the first/only clip. Keep the AR-default USDZ to a clean looping idle or walk.

---

## 6. Handoff checklist for Yash

```
LITTLE SUPERCLAWS — MESHY RIG + ANIMATE (5 chars × walk/dance/idle)

PREP
[ ] Confirm each GLB: single textured mesh, A/T-pose, limbs separated, face pointing +Z, upright & symmetrical.
[ ] Check tri/face count. Any model >300k faces -> decimate to ~150-250k (Meshy Remesh API or Blender), re-verify texture/UVs.
[ ] Host each GLB at a public URL (or use data URI) for the API.

RIG (per character)
[ ] POST /openapi/v1/rigging  { model_url, height_meters: 1.7 }  -> save rig_task_id
[ ] Poll GET /openapi/v1/rigging/:id until SUCCEEDED
[ ] Eyeball preview deform; if 422/misplaced -> fix pose/+Z/symmetry & re-run (Mixamo fallback if stuck)
[ ] Save rigged_character_glb_url

ANIMATE (3 clips per character — action_ids)
[ ] Clawd:   walk 121, dance 79, idle 36
[ ] Nessa:   walk 107, dance 66, idle 255
[ ] Deirdre: walk 106, dance 74, idle 12
[ ] Decklan: walk 55,  dance 82, idle 11
[ ] Gerald:  walk 123, dance 22, idle 36
[ ] POST /openapi/v1/animations { rig_task_id, action_id, post_process:{operation_type:"change_fps", fps:30} }
[ ] For the AR-default clip add post_process {operation_type:"fbx2usdz"} -> grab processed_usdz_url

EXPORT / DELIVER (per character)
[ ] Download GLB for walk/dance/idle (+ base rigged GLB), FBX as fallback
[ ] Download USDZ for AR-default clip
[ ] Keep Meshy default scale (2cm sizing handled at conversion)
[ ] (Optional) merge 3 clips into one multi-clip GLB for model-viewer clip switching

NOTES
- Auth: Authorization: Bearer ${MESHY_API_KEY} on every call. Base: https://api.meshy.ai
- GLB only on input, <=300k faces, .glb. Result URLs expire -> download immediately.
- Tasks are async: POST returns id, poll GET :id (or stream :id/stream) to SUCCEEDED.
- Watch 429 rate limits; credits refunded on FAILED tasks (~5 credits/rig).
- Docs: https://docs.meshy.ai/en/api/rigging  |  /animation  |  /animation-library (full action_id list)
```
